critics.palate: Spearmint, chocolate and cream (mint-chocolate-ice-cream feel) plus tobacco leaf, coffee and cinnamon sugar; good mouthfeel.
critics.finish: Medium; turns sweeter with vanilla, stewed fruit and warming cinnamon stick.

critics.nose: Wildflower honey, pear and vanilla seasoned with nutmeg.
critics.palate: Delicate and spice-forward; clove and dill with vanilla, malty honey, apple and pear.
critics.finish: Clove and dill spice lead.
critics.summary: Graded A- (letter grade); reviewer's favorite New Riff release at the time.

critics.nose: Richly spiced like a fresh cinnamon loaf, with vanilla and restrained virgin oak.
critics.palate: Savory peppery warmth, then toasted rye and sourdough bread, honey, clove and demerara sugar.
critics.finish: Light and fairly quick, without dill funk.
critics.summary: Co-reviewer Aengus McCloud scored it 6/10 on the same page.

facts.cask: New charred oak

new-riff-malted-rye.notes: Sources describe a 6-year, 100-proof bottled-in-bond malted rye; input lists NAS/90 proof/undisclosed mash, which looks wrong. Check which bottle the user has (New Riff also sells sherry-finish and 8-yr malted ryes).

producer.nose: Cinnamon, dried cherry, light leather
producer.palate: Warming spice, vanilla, caramel, chocolate-coated peppermint
producer.summary: Rye-forward Kentucky straight bourbon aged onsite in old warehouses.

green-river-bourbon.notes: No critic review found (guessed Breaking Bourbon URLs 404). Age not stated on page.

producer.palate: Peach, apricot, cinnamon, confection notes
producer.finish: Lingering, rich, hazelnut and honey hints
producer.summary: Smooth wheated bourbon; SF World Spirits Competition gold claimed.

critics.nose: Fresh bread, creamed corn, summer fruit; low intensity
critics.palate: Caramel, vanilla, subtle leather, soft char, wheat, light pepper
critics.finish: White pepper, soft wheat, baked bread
critics.summary: Average, drinkable wheated bourbon valued for $35 price.

producer.nose: Cinnamon, dried cherry, light leather
producer.palate: Warming spice, vanilla, caramel, chocolate-coated peppermint
producer.summary: Uncut barrel-strength bourbon hand-blended from select barrels.

critics.nose: Vanilla, caramel, oak, leather, cinnamon
critics.palate: Caramel cream candy, brown sugar, thick creamy texture, dark fruit, honey, char
critics.finish: Layered oak, dark fruit, rye spice; memorable
critics.summary: Well-rounded and good value at about $50.

facts.age: Blend of 5-7 year bourbons per Breaking Bourbon

green-river-full-proof.notes: Age claim from a single critic page.

producer.nose: Bright citrus, fresh mint, rye spice, subtle sweetness
producer.palate: Orange peel, spearmint, black pepper, vanilla, graham cracker
producer.finish: Medium; rye spice, herbal tea, soft oak
producer.summary: Kentucky straight rye.
Billed as a high-rye bourbon with a burst of rye spice; estate distilled; IWSC 2023 gold. Page has no stage-by-stage tasting notes.

critics.nose: Tangerine, vanilla and eggnog up front, with pine at the edges.
critics.palate: Smooth and round; coconut and toasted walnut, a dusting of anise, lighter pine/cedar wood rather than oak.
critics.finish: Strong vanilla with surprising sherry and grape notes.

critics.nose: Somewhat closed; sweet and earthy with malty corn, wood shavings and caramel popcorn.
critics.palate: Thick, syrupy and gentle; apple peel, custard, vanilla and crème brûlée, well balanced.
critics.finish: Medium; rye bursts, drying oak and honey.

bardstown-bourbon-co-origin-series-bourb.notes: Producer page gives specs and a marketing summary but no nose/palate/finish notes; critic notes are for the exact 6yr 96-proof expression.

producer.summary: Estate-distilled bourbon with an unusually high 39% wheat mash, said to draw a lot of wood sugar; SFWSC 2025 gold. No stage-by-stage tasting notes on page.

critics.nose: Apricot, orange zest, vanilla cream, white pepper.
critics.palate: Buttercream frosting, dried apricot, butterscotch candy, toffee.
critics.finish: Warming; cinnamon, allspice, light leather.
critics.summary: Sweet, flavorful wheater; considered good value at ~$50 MSRP.

critics.nose: Layers of vanilla, amaretti cookie, bright orange and oak with brown sugar and toffee.
critics.palate: Baked bread and apricot jam, then vanilla, light baking spice, cherry, oak, a touch of maple and orange.
critics.finish: Warm and juicy, slightly sweet, moderate length.

bardstown-bourbon-co-origin-high-wheat.notes: Producer page lacks stage-by-stage notes; mash bill matches producer and Breaking Bourbon.

producer.summary: Straight rye finished in custom hybrid barrels with alternating toasted cherry wood and oak staves; pitched for classic cocktails. No stage-by-stage notes on page.

critics.nose: Nougat, marzipan, aged oak, barrel char, rye spice, leather.
critics.palate: Rye grain, charred oak, leather, baking and Mexican chocolate, dried fig.
critics.finish: Bold rye spice, dry oak, Mexican chocolate, a little leather, lingering heat.
critics.summary: Well-made first in-house rye; the cherry-wood barrel adds distinctive flavor for rye fans.

critics.nose: Grassy juniper and fern with nutmeg, black pepper and apricot.
critics.palate: Dried apricot and cherry, prominent oak, anise, lavender, corn and clove.

facts.age: 6 years (producer); Breaking Bourbon lists its 2023 sample at 5 years 8 months
facts.cask: Finished in toasted cherry wood and oak hybrid barrels

bardstown-bourbon-co-origin-rye.notes: Mash bill per producer and Breaking Bourbon; cherry-wood finish confirmed by producer and Whiskey Wash. Age statement differs slightly between sources.

bardstown-bourbon-co-discovery-series.notes: Discovery Series is a numbered run of distinct blends (producer lists proofs from roughly 110.8 to 118.1, not 90); input does not name the release, so no expression matched.

bardstown-bourbon-co-collaborative-serie.notes: Collaborative/Barrel Finish series covers many different partner finishes; input does not name one, so no expression matched.

producer.nose: Sweet baking spice, oak and dark fruit.
producer.palate: Smooth and sweet, moving to tobacco and bramble red-black fruit with a hint of leather and smoke.
producer.finish: Long and rye-led with warm, oaky sweetness that lasts.
producer.summary: Deep amber, unfiltered; positioned as a spicier counterpart to the distillery's wheated bourbon.

critics.nose: Strong caramel with candy corn, fresh grass, cinnamon roll and raspberry cream, ending on oak.
critics.palate: Rich caramel, butterscotch, brown sugar, vanilla extract and raspberry; faint mint late.
critics.finish: Turns to cinnamon, bitter chocolate, rye spice, char and black pepper, then nutty almond; dries out with lingering mint.
critics.summary: Delivers on the high-rye promise but the sharp, peppery close may not suit everyone; value questioned.

critics.nose: Very herbaceous with a distinct mint note.
critics.palate: Gentle spice and a menthol lift while staying balanced.
critics.summary: Praised the integration of flavor and alcohol; calls the distillery one to watch.

critics.nose: Caramel candy, pronounced herbal rye, pepper, floral vanilla and a trace of wood smoke.
critics.palate: Honeyed sweetness with assertive rye spice, peppercorn, brown sugar and mint, developing charred astringency.

wilderness-trail-high-rye-bourbon.notes: Producer site shows identical tasting copy on its high-rye bourbon and rye pages. Mash bill per Paste and The Whiskey Jug (Breaking Bourbon lists 25% rye). Proof/BIB per producer whiskeys page.

producer.nose: Sweet vanilla and charred oak.
producer.palate: Caramel and vanilla leading into oak, cinnamon and blood orange, with a palate-coating texture.
producer.finish: Long and sweet; oak spice, toffee and dark fruit.
producer.summary: Sweet-mash wheated bourbon with reduced corn and more 'middle grains'; billed as the first bottled-in-bond wheated sweet-mash bourbon since Prohibition.

critics.nose: Cherry and slightly tart blackberry with gingerbread, cinnamon and molasses cookie.
critics.palate: Soft entry; brown sugar, cinnamon, toasted oak, cherry cordial, clove and cola spice.

critics.nose: Toasted graham cracker with apricot jam, brown sugar, cinnamon, clove and musty oak.
critics.palate: Sweet and fruity with honey and caramel; punches above its age.
critics.finish: Warm and honeyed with more wood, though it fades a bit early.
critics.summary: Letter grade B+ (no numeric scale).

wilderness-trail-wheated-bourbon.notes: Mash bill per Paste and The Whiskey Reviewer; proof/BIB per producer whiskeys page.

producer.nose: Sweet baking spice, oak and dark fruit.
producer.palate: Smooth and sweet, moving to tobacco and bramble red-black fruit with a hint of leather and smoke.
producer.finish: Long and rye-led with warm, oaky sweetness that lasts.
producer.summary: Marketed as 'the bourbon drinker's rye': lower-rye, higher-corn custom mash entered at a low 100-105 barrel proof.

critics.nose: Caraway rye bread, peppermint, florals, dark chocolate and spicy oak.
critics.palate: Bold rye with caraway, pepper, rye bread, honey and herbal notes, with modest corn sweetness.

wilderness-trail-rye.notes: Producer tasting copy is identical to its high-rye bourbon page, so it may not be specific to the rye. Mash bill 56/33/11 appears only in Paste (one source), so left null.

producer.summary: Distillery bills it as a four-grain bourbon with a balanced mash bill, the official spirit of the 2017 and 2024 total solar eclipses, made in limited quantities. No nose/palate/finish notes on the page.

critics.nose: Caramel, fresh raspberry, prune, Concord grape and brown sugar.
critics.palate: Vanilla and caramel with light clove and white pepper.
critics.finish: Butterscotch, burnt orange peel and rye spice.
critics.summary: 2024 release reviewed (listed as 2 yrs 6 mos, 100 proof). Approachable, fun commemorative branding, but fairly simple given its youth. Rated 2.5 on Breaking Bourbon's own rating scale (scale not captured).

critics.nose: Plenty of graham cracker plus a touch of honey, turning sweeter and almost floral toward the back.
critics.palate: Bitter orange and orange peel develop over a honeyed base, moving toward tannin.
critics.finish: Tannic and dry with a sweet honeyed lift and a slight oiliness that softens the mouthfeel for a young whiskey.
critics.summary: Young 100-proof bourbon; reviewer scored it 7/10 at about $48.

casey-jones-total-eclipse-bourbon.notes: Input age 'At least 4 years' conflicts with producer ('minimum 2 years') and Breaking Bourbon (2y6m); age set from producer. Producer page has no tasting notes. A WhiskyCast rating page (89, dated Nov 2023, 2 yrs) was excluded: its date predates the 2024 release so batch (possibly 2017) is unclear and scale was not explicit.

producer.nose: Vanilla, caramel and light oak.
producer.palate: Smooth and balanced with brown sugar, vanilla and gentle spice.
producer.summary: Notes relayed by retailer Wooden Cork and attributed there to the distillery; Kentucky straight small-batch bourbon from Master Distiller Arlon Casey Jones. Proof not stated on the page.

casey-jones-small-batch-bourbon.notes: Could not confirm a 90-proof Casey Jones Small Batch. Other Small Batch releases found were different proofs and excluded: 2019 first release at 104.2 proof (Distillery Trail) and a 108-proof bottling (People's Bourbon Review). Current distillery small-batch product is Revere at 100 proof, also excluded. Retailer notes may not match the 90-proof bottle.

casey-jones-barrel-cut-bourbon.notes: Distillery's Barrel Cut line (Single Barrel 100-115 proof, Double Barrel 80-117 proof) is described as a corn-and-cane Kentucky specialty spirit, not bourbon, and no 90-proof Barrel Cut bourbon was found. Possible data error in input; nothing recorded.

producer.nose: Citrus, cedar and honeysuckle over balanced spicy oak.
producer.palate: Caramel and toasted oak first, then fruit, floral and oak notes.
producer.finish: Sweet citrus, floral and sweet oak play against dry cocoa, cinnamon and spicy oak.
producer.summary: Producer stresses it is distilled in-house (never sourced), sweet mash, barrel proof with no water added, and not chill-filtered.

peerless-small-batch-bourbon.notes: Producer page states barrel proof but no specific proof/age; batch proof varies so input 109 not verified. No critic review fetched (tool quota exhausted).

producer.nose: Sweet oak with orange zest and cedar, then tobacco and herbs.
producer.palate: Honeyed sweetness shifting quickly to cinnamon and spicy oak, with leather adding earthiness and a big body.
producer.finish: Viscous, with sweet toasted oak and dry cocoa.
producer.summary: Matured in two separate barrels for two full barrel extractions; bottled at barrel proof.

critics.nose: Medium-roast coffee, semi-sweet chocolate and cherry, plus brown sugar, torched orange peel and black tea.
critics.palate: Dark brown sugar and cacao up front, a flash of orange and cherry syrup, then burnt toffee and vanilla bean.
critics.finish: Chocolate-orange with growing orange oil, lingering vanilla, and cardamom, clove and nutmeg.
critics.summary: Batch 15CS241C6 (2022) at 54.2% ABV. Reviewer admired it more than enjoyed it, calling it frustratingly close to great, and questioned value at about $87. No numeric score captured.

facts.cask: Matured in two separate barrels (double oak)

peerless-double-oak-bourbon.notes: Barrel-proof product; proof varies by batch. Critic batch was 54.2% ABV (108.4 proof) vs input 109. Excluded a Bourbon Culture review (7.7/10) because it covered a 108-proof single-barrel store pick, not the standard release.

producer.palate: Balanced; sweet maple, brown sugar and light citrus sweetness.
producer.finish: A touch of oak with no throat burn.
producer.summary: Producer pitches it as a smooth sipping rye, bottled at barrel proof, non-chill-filtered, made with a sweet mash process.

critics.nose: Honey and spice up front, then vanilla, apple and charred oak; little alcohol heat.
critics.palate: Bold oak with warm honey, caramelized pear, baking spice and a hint of milk chocolate.
critics.finish: Vanilla and sweet orange moving to butterscotch and hickory smoke, with lingering spice and pumpkin.
critics.summary: Very positive; calls it a benchmark premium rye for sipping or cocktails. A numeric 10 is shown but the scale is not stated, so score omitted.

critics.nose: Sugar cookie, maple, buttered cinnamon bread.
critics.palate: Caramel creme, lemon frosting, vanilla extract.
critics.finish: Long and rich: English toffee, charred oak, cola.
critics.summary: Called an exceptional, rich and complex pour that tastes pricier than it is; qualitative rating only. Reviewed bottle was 109.6 proof.

peerless-small-batch-rye.notes: Producer page gives no proof/age/mash bill, only that it is barrel proof and non-chill-filtered; barrel proof varies by batch (one reviewer's bottle was 109.6 vs input 110). Producer notes are not split into nose/palate; mapped from one descriptive sentence.

producer.nose: Sweet seasoned oak with orange zest; robust.
producer.palate: Warm molasses and earthy cinnamon at first, shifting to bright florals and smoky, earthy herbs.
producer.finish: Candied smoke as bright and dark notes play off each other.
producer.summary: Straight rye aged in two new oak casks (from the Peerless online shop). The distillery says it selects barrels with prominent grain, fruit and herbaceous notes for the second cask.

critics.nose: Dark caramel, toasted oak, graham cracker and rye spice.
critics.palate: Thick, oily; rye and cinnamon spice fading into oak, dark chocolate and dark caramel, then a return of cinnamon.
critics.finish: Lingering dark chocolate, black pepper, rye spice, late mint.
critics.summary: Praised the balance of sweet and spice and deep flavors. Bottle reviewed was barrel R150922109, 109.6 proof, stated 5 years old.

facts.cask: Two new oak casks (double oaked)

peerless-double-oak-rye.notes: Producer pages state barrel proof but give no specific proof/age/mash bill; input 108 proof is unverified. The sole critic review covers a specific barrel at 109.6 proof, which may differ from other releases.

critics.nose: Ripe cherry and a little citrus over vanilla and dry oak, hints of buttered popcorn and honey.
critics.palate: Honey and caramel against spice and zesty citrus; fairly thin mouthfeel.
critics.finish: Rye spice building, then cinnamon, buttered popcorn, vanilla and caramel; lingering spice.
critics.summary: Slightly above average and distinctive, but the liquid falls short of the showpiece bottle. Batch 19C25, 94 proof.

critics.nose: Hot spirity vapor with wood and maple underneath.
critics.palate: Immediate rye spice, not sweet, heavy oak, a hint of cayenne over a neutral corn base.
critics.finish: Long and warming as it fades.
critics.summary: Attractive gift bottle but ordinary liquid. A 5 is shown without a stated scale, so score omitted.

facts.cask: Barrel entry proof 115

willett-pot-still-reserve.notes: Producer page has no tasting notes. It currently lists a wheated mash bill (corn/wheat/barley), yet both critics describe rye spice; the reviewed bottles (2020, 2024) may predate or differ from the current recipe.

producer.summary: Producer describes a cask-strength blend of two rye mash bills meant to evoke a historic Maryland-style rye, balancing fruit and spice; no formal tasting notes.

critics.nose: Floral, botanical and sweet; caramel apple, caramel popcorn, burnt toffee over honey and rye bread.
critics.palate: Warm raisin, menthol and spice with green tea giving a slightly medicinal note, plus light cherry and citrus.
critics.finish: More botanicals and spice, toasted grain, black pepper, lingering dryness.
critics.summary: Called unique and surprisingly complex. Rated 3.5 on the site's own scale (scale not stated on the page, so score omitted). Reviewed bottle 111.2 proof.

critics.nose: Licorice, honey, dark berries, anise, fennel, caraway, citrus and herbal botanicals.
critics.palate: Spicy, herbal sweetness: licorice, honey, fennel, roasted oak, cinnamon, vanilla; likened to lightly sweetened lemon tea.
critics.finish: Herbal, sweet and tannic with honey, licorice, baked bread and mint, moving to black tea and eucalyptus.
critics.summary: Rated 'Top Shelf' (qualitative); dense, unique herbal rye. Reviewed bottle 56.6% ABV.

facts.mash_bill: Blend: 90% of a 74% rye / 11% corn / 15% barley mash and 10% of a 51% rye / 34% corn / 15% barley mash
facts.cask: Barrel entry proof 110; bottled at cask strength

willett-family-estate-4-year-rye.notes: Producer gives no tasting notes or bottling proof; 110 is barrel entry proof. Cask strength varies by batch (critics' bottles were 111.2 and ~113.2 proof vs input 110). Mash bill percentages read from the producer page layout.

producer.summary: Producer calls it a robust, smooth bourbon; no formal tasting notes.

critics.nose: Rye-like spice, vanilla and caramel; dusty, musty warehouse character.
critics.palate: Sweet start, spice-forward with oak, vanilla, caramel and dusty notes.
critics.finish: Fairly smooth and sweet; dark chocolate and coffee.
critics.summary: Average of two tasters just below their recommend threshold; worth trying at a bar, questionable value. Reviewed at 114.3 proof.

critics.nose: Wax and corn, wood, straw, honey, herbs and dust, dried apricot and papaya.
critics.palate: Complex: vanilla, oatcake, leather, spices, sunflower seeds, dried fruit; proof well integrated.
critics.finish: Long, focused and creamy.
critics.summary: A personal favorite of the reviewer; no score. Reviewed at 57.15% ABV.

facts.cask: Barrel entry proof 125

noah-s-mill.notes: No producer tasting notes. Film Whiskey review was recorded 2021 and posted 2024; older Noah's Mill was sourced whiskey, so profile may differ by era.

producer.summary: Producer notes the label honors the creek on the family distillery and describes a smooth, approachable whiskey; no formal tasting notes.

critics.nose: Very sweet: caramel, brown sugar, raisin, rose petal, vanilla, honey; slight lighter-fluid note.
critics.palate: Smoky, cigar-like and corn-forward; bitter and tart.
critics.finish: Hot at first, medium-long, smoky with a hint of cinnamon.
critics.summary: Disappointing for the price versus peers. Reviewed at 50.05% ABV.

critics.nose: Lots of raisin, creamy vanilla, faint dark chocolate.
critics.palate: Aged oak with rye pepper and spice, nutty aftertaste.
critics.finish: Modest, oak and sweet spice.
critics.summary: Above average but one-dimensional and arguably overpriced. A 6 is shown without a stated scale; year not stated.

facts.cask: Barrel entry proof 125

rowan-s-creek.notes: No producer tasting notes. Critic reviews (2019 and undated) likely reflect older, possibly sourced batches.

producer.summary: Producer says it was developed by Thompson Willett in the 1960s, with a retro look and rye-forward flavor; no formal tasting notes.

critics.nose: Caramel, cinnamon, marzipan, light oak spice.
critics.palate: Caramel, peanut and cinnamon up front; midpalate turns to allspice, clove and oak.
critics.finish: Long, spicy, slightly dry and well balanced.
critics.summary: Called a hidden gem that drinks easily neat for its proof. Reviewed at 101 proof.

critics.nose: Mint, grain, honeydew melon, allspice.
critics.palate: Dry, grain-forward with mint, brown sugar, oak and spice.
critics.finish: Warm, spicy, decent length.
critics.summary: Liked it as a well-integrated, non-oaky bourbon; no numeric score. Reviewed at 101 proof.

facts.mash_bill: Blend: 65% of a 52% corn / 38% rye / 10% barley mash and 35% of a 72% corn / 13% rye / 15% barley mash
facts.cask: Barrel entry proof 125

johnny-drum-private-stock.notes: PROOF MISMATCH: producer page lists 101 proof / 50.5% ABV, not the input's 90 proof / 45%; all critics reviewed the 101-proof bottle. Critic reviews (2013, 2016) predate the current Willett-distilled blend.

producer.summary: Willett product page lists proof/ABV and a general line about Kentucky limestone water; no nose/palate/finish notes given.

critics.nose: Black tea, cedar, mustiness, oak, spice, vanilla and a sooty note.
critics.palate: Eucalyptus and earth, more vanilla, cherry, with rye grain moving forward.
critics.finish: Salty with maple syrup and woody, forest-like character.
critics.summary: Retailer-written tasting notes, not an independent critic; listing gives 53.5% ABV.

pure-kentucky-xo.notes: Input says 90 proof/45% but Willett page and Hi-Time list 107 proof/53.5%; input proof likely wrong. Willett page mash-bill figures are garbled (one sums >100%), so omitted. Hi-Time claims 11 years old (retailer only, not recorded as fact). Total Wine page had only producer marketing copy, no notes.

producer.summary: Willett says the blend of two mash bills yields a mellow, balanced flavor; no separate nose/palate/finish notes.

critics.nose: Sawdust and hay, very dry with splintery oak and dry corn husk; corn syrup and acetone after air.
critics.palate: Full-bodied and woody with birch beer, roasted chestnut, cola and light cinnamon.
critics.finish: Medium-short and drying; late cola and black licorice sweetness, fades quickly.
critics.summary: Liked the birch-beer note but found it shallow with off-notes; recommends passing. Water brought out almond/marzipan.

critics.nose: Slight ethanol, sweet corn, light vanilla and sugar; youthful, caramel with air.
critics.palate: Salty peanut, tobacco, earthiness, black pepper and leather; little sweetness.
critics.finish: Light and dry with slightly bitter peanut and gentle warmth.
critics.summary: Notes an unusual saltiness; reviewer leaned positive and suggests it suits cocktails.

facts.mash_bill: Blend of two Willett mash bills; page lists 72% corn/13% rye/15% barley (125 barrel-entry proof) and 79% corn/7% rye/14% barley (107 barrel-entry proof)

kentucky-vintage.notes: Producer offers only a one-line descriptor. Page also shows a stray '85%' figure of unclear meaning; mash bills recorded as the two cleanly listed sets. Critic reviews (2016, 2021) may predate a shift to Willett-distilled whiskey; both reviewers mention an unverified ~10-year rumor.

producer.summary: Willett page calls it the original family mash bill and notes Kentucky-only distribution; no tasting notes given.

critics.nose: Molasses, caramel, mint and cherry cough syrup; youthful with some chemical notes.
critics.palate: Thin in body and flavor; caramel over faint butterscotch and oak, underdeveloped.
critics.finish: Low burn with faint clove, cinnamon and pepper.
critics.summary: Easy-drinking but bland; sees promise in Willett's own distillate but little else. Score scale not clearly stated, so not recorded.

facts.cask: 125 barrel-entry proof

old-bardstown-bottled-in-bond.notes: No producer tasting notes. Only critic review fetched is from 2016, early in the Willett-distilled era; current bottlings are likely older. Bourbon Guy 2025 revisit was rate-limited (429).

producer.nose: Warm vanilla and honey over a rich caramel sweetness.
producer.palate: Smooth, warm and sweet; a light rye spice, with caramel and honey rounded out by oak and char.
producer.summary: Tribute to Heaven Hill's original 1939 bottled-in-bond release; aged 7 years, three years beyond the bonded minimum.

critics.nose: Vanilla, caramel and aged oak up front, with background leather, tobacco and honey; a bit light for the proof.
critics.palate: Seasoned oak and spice lead, then savory tobacco and leather against graham cracker and butterscotch; light, somewhat dry mouthfeel.
critics.finish: Medium to long; cinnamon spice and caramel with oak, cherry and vanilla, dryness easing toward sweetness.
critics.summary: A decent, classic-profile bourbon, but weaker value at its roughly $40 price versus competitors (score given as 2.5 of 5 barrels).

critics.nose: Vanilla, warm oak and caramel with dried apricot and banana, plus leather, citrus, toasted nuts and some ethanol.
critics.palate: Rich and balanced; caramel and honey open, then corn warmth and rye structure, with oak and char.
critics.finish: Medium; toasty oak, black pepper and lasting caramel.
critics.summary: Strong value; recommended as an easy bar staple for newcomers and seasoned drinkers alike.

heaven-hill-bottled-in-bond-7-year.notes: Producer page did not state mash bill; Breaking Bourbon's review lists 78% corn / 12% malted barley / 10% rye (matches input) but facts.source_url points to producer page, so mash_bill left null. Breaking Bourbon review is from 2019 (original ~$40 relaunch).

critics.nose: Caramel-heavy dark sweets, oak, French vanilla, dark fruit and sweet cream; hints of maple and grain.
critics.palate: Creamy caramel, oak, toasted corn and spice with light sweetness and leather.
critics.finish: Long and spicy with dark fruit, sweetness and wood.
critics.summary: Strong value; pleasant neat and robust in cocktails, medium body.

critics.nose: Soft and sweet: sweet corn, cherry syrup, marshmallow, mild nutty oak.
critics.palate: Cherry lozenge and caramel frosting, then cinnamon, clove and brown sugar with moderate burn.
critics.finish: Medium-long and warming with mild tannic dryness, vanilla frosting and faint oak.
critics.summary: Called it a quintessential, possibly among the best sub-$20 bourbons; good for cocktails.

critics.nose: Toffee almond, lightly roasted corn, slight floral note, then nut butter and clove/cinnamon/nutmeg.
critics.palate: Honey-nut cereal, roasted peanut, ground pepper, caramel, peanut brittle, light brown sugar.
critics.finish: Lingering pepper, drying wood and roasted peanut.
critics.summary: Solid, reliable budget bonded bourbon, neat or mixed. Bottle filled early 2020 per laser code.

evan-williams-bottled-in-bond.notes: Heaven Hill product page not reachable (www robots failure; non-www slugs 404). Facts from critic page; input mash bill not confirmed by any fetched source. Scotch Noob page shows a graphic rating whose scale was unclear, so not recorded.

producer.nose: Dark caramel with sweet oak and charred wood.
producer.palate: Lush and spicy; oak with honey, apple and orange.
producer.summary: Heaven Hill notes each bottle carries its barrel-entry vintage date, bottling year and barrel number.

critics.nose: Wood varnish, dusty cereal, bright vanilla cream, sour cherry, cream soda; fresh oak.
critics.palate: Classic oak, caramel and nutty Heaven Hill profile with red fruit and citrus, like orange marmalade and walnut.
critics.finish: Medium; French toast, oak and cherry cordial with dry warming spice.
critics.summary: 2015 vintage (bottled 2024). Solid, approachable value. Page shows 88 but scale not stated, so not recorded.

critics.nose: Mild and sweet: wood, grainy bread, rye and fruit with leather, pepper, cinnamon.
critics.palate: Caramel, rye, leather, wood with apple, pepper and toasted nuts.

critics.summary: Quoted on US importer's 2023 page.

klein-constantia-sauvignon-blanc.notes: Producer page current vintage (2025 listed) vs critics on 2023; elevage details differ by vintage. ABV not found.

producer.palate: Explosive mix of floral, fruit, saline and herbal notes; sweetness balanced by acidity.
producer.summary: Half the blend aged six months on lees in neutral 500L French oak (2023 spec sheet).

critics.palate: Zippy, hints of chive blossom and white pepper.
critics.summary: Only a truncated free snippet; score paywalled. Listed at $17.

facts.cask: 50% on lees in neutral 500L French oak, 6 months

mulderbosch-sauvignon-blanc.notes: Producer notes 2023; critic note is a thin 2021 Wine Spectator snippet.

critics.nose: Passion fruit and pear with honeydew.
critics.palate: Medium-bodied, zesty; green tea, lime, white grapefruit, chalky minerality, tonic.
critics.finish: Dry, extended.

critics.palate: Stony, green herb, white pepper and briny mineral with tropical fruit.
critics.finish: Flinty.
critics.summary: Fresh and zesty, medium-bodied.
4.5 stars / 94 points relayed by retailer; youthful vigour on a dusty-grassy base. Tim Atkin 92 also listed.

facts.cask: Cool stainless-steel fermentation with extended lees contact (per retailer)

neil-ellis-groenekloof-sauvignon-blanc.notes: Producer site unreachable (robots/timeout). A retailer (vinty.co.za) shows winery-style notes for 2024 but attribution unclear, so not used as producer notes. Critics span 2019-2024; ABV 13% from MacLean 2019.

producer.summary: Estate aims for minerality and palate complexity over pungent varietal aroma; texture from clay-shale, openness from granite, saline brightness from sandstone.

critics.nose: Flint, white flowers, lemon sorbet.
critics.summary: Delicate style with a salty, seashell tone; 92 per producer page.

critics.palate: Crisp and linear, finely delineated.
critics.finish: Precise and sapid.

critics.nose: Wet stone and struck match.
critics.palate: Passion fruit and lemongrass, racy acidity.

facts.cask: 8% barrel fermented in neutral oak

southern-right-sauvignon-blanc.notes: All 2024 vintage. Producer page gives style philosophy rather than nose/palate notes. ABV 13.51% from model summary of producer page.

producer.summary: Blend of early and late pickings showing passion fruit, nettle and minerality; built to age 2-4 years. Night-harvested, 100 days on lees.

critics.nose: Smoky and aromatic without pungency.
critics.palate: Textured with refreshing acidity.
critics.summary: Distinct from Marlborough-style Sauvignon.

facts.cask: Stainless; ~100 days lees contact

springfield-special-cuv-e-sauvignon-blan.notes: Producer page is 2026 vintage; Decanter review 2021 (12.5%). Waitrose (retailer) also lists gooseberry/lime/citrus at 13%. Producer note is a summary, not split nose/palate.

producer.nose: Fresh apricot, ripe pear, lime and orange blossom with fynbos and dried herbs.
producer.palate: Bright, refreshing acidity.
producer.summary: Standard estate Sauvignon Blanc (distinct from Reserve, Noordhoek and Isliedh bottlings).

cape-point-vineyards-sauvignon-blanc.notes: Vintage not stated on producer page. Critic reviews found were for Noordhoek or Reserve bottlings (different expressions), so skipped; strictlywine.co.uk returned 403.

producer.nose: Lime zest, gooseberry, passion fruit, white peach with cut herbs, snap pea and fynbos.
producer.palate: Bright, focused, textured; grapefruit, ripe kiwi, green melon.
producer.summary: DMZ Sauvignon Blanc; cool extended ferment, lees time with stirring (2025).

critics.summary: 2020 vintage, South Africa Report 2021; score only.

critics.palate: Lively, with light, plump juiciness.
critics.summary: Truncated free snippet; score paywalled. Listed at $18.

facts.cask: Stainless with lees aging and stirring

demorgenzon-sauvignon-blanc.notes: Assumed the DMZ Sauvignon Blanc (estate's SB label). Producer notes 2025; critics 2020-2021, thin.

producer.nose: Dark stone fruit with caramelized sugar and toasted oak.
producer.palate: Big oak balanced by dark vanilla and fruit.
producer.finish: Velvety, long and complex, with caramelized barrel character and baking spice.
producer.summary: Official Maker's Mark notes as relayed by the KY Supply Co. retailer blog (2023 release article), not fetched from makersmark.com.

critics.nose: Deeper and more pungent than other Maker's expressions; berry/mulberry fruit with mint and rosemary.
critics.palate: Dark caramel and chocolate, then baked berry, apple and apricot with brown sugar; no drying astringency.
critics.finish: Sweet, maple-syrup tinged, long without lingering too heavily; complexity tapers a bit.
critics.summary: Called it close to flawless and the new flagship of the range; inaugural 2023 release at 115.7 proof.

critics.nose: Toffee and somewhat astringent sawdust, buttered toast, clove and orange.
critics.palate: Dark chocolate and bitter orange moving to butterscotch, tobacco and cinnamon, then bitter oak with caramel and faint mint.
critics.finish: Oak-dominated and hotter than expected, briefly sweetened by the wheated mash.
critics.summary: Found it too oak-heavy; suited to fans of double-oaked, overproof styles. 2023 release (115.74 proof).

facts.age: Blend of 11- and 12-year-old bourbon (sources disagree on the split)

ks-maker-s-mark-cellar-aged-ksbw.notes: Matches 2023 inaugural release at 115.7 proof. Age split conflicts: KY Supply says 70% 11yr/30% 12yr, VinePair says 13% 11yr/87% 12yr. Producer notes are retailer-relayed; makersmark.com product page 404.

critics.nose: Caramel and cinnamon up front with corn sweetness, black pepper and green apple.
critics.palate: Seasoned oak, cinnamon, brown sugar, burnt orange peel, vanilla, prune and leather.
critics.finish: Warm and lingering; cinnamon, baking and rye spice over charred oak and molasses.
critics.summary: Calls it a must-have for its proof, flavor and value.

critics.nose: Sharp rye prickle, baking spice, caramel and baked apple with a youthful grainy undertone.
critics.palate: Cinnamon and spiced honey with tarragon and mint; thick but hot.
critics.finish: Lingering peppery burn; vanilla and toffee under heat, tobacco tannins and char.
critics.summary: Excellent value at about $20 but would benefit from more age.

ks-old-grand-dad-114-ksbw.notes: No producer notes: oldgranddad.com redirects to a domain-sale page. Older 2014 Breaking Bourbon review skipped (score unclear).

critics.nose: Light char and oak with fresh bread and caramel.
critics.palate: Earthy cocoa, leather and apple with mild pepper; char, burnt sugar and gentle oak.
critics.finish: Burnt sugar with very mild oak.
critics.summary: Amateur blog review of the 86-proof bottling; praised its smoothness and value. No numeric score.

ks-evan-williams-1783-small-batch-ksbw.notes: Kansas label is the older 86-proof version; brand moved to 90 proof (~2021) and most reviews (Breaking Bourbon, The Whisky Study) cover 90 proof, so they were excluded. Producer pages 404/blocked. Only critic is an amateur blog.

critics.nose: Sweet vanilla first, then orange and vibrant oak, marshmallow, maple, milk chocolate, baking spice.
critics.palate: Orange candy and warm vanilla with oak, bread, pear, coriander, cinnamon and maple.
critics.finish: Clean, not aggressive, sweet and moderately fading.
critics.summary: 2024 release reviewed at 107 proof, 6 years old.

critics.nose: Sweet popcorn, white peach, light grain, white pepper, faint oak.
critics.palate: Rye spice, hot cross buns, mixed peppercorn, tannic oak, light brown sugar.
critics.finish: Bold rye spice, leather, dry oak, green peppercorn, lingering dry spice.
critics.summary: 2024 release at 107 proof; interesting concept but premium price limits appeal.

critics.nose: Spiced nuts, ballpark peanuts, new oak, baking spice and dried apricot.
critics.palate: Layered rye spice with cinnamon stick, tannic oak and grilled glazed peach.
critics.finish: Brown sugar giving way to bold rye spice, peppery oak and leather; dry with building heat.
critics.summary: 2025 release at 105 proof; $100 price called hard to justify. Rating not clearly captured.

ks-heaven-hill-grain-to-glass-ksbw.notes: PROOF MISMATCH: Kansas label says 100 proof, but reviewed releases are 107 (2024) and 105 (2025); no 100-proof edition found. Critics cover the same product line at different batch proofs. No producer notes found (heavenhilldistillery.com blocked).

producer.nose: Fresh ginger, butterscotch and salt spray.
producer.palate: Salted caramel, chocolate and tropical fruit.
producer.summary: Official notes from the Jefferson's Ocean page; barrels are aged aboard ships.

critics.nose: Mature bourbon: spice, caramel, vanilla, brown sugar, cherry, orange zest, dark honey, oak.
critics.palate: Bourbon spice and dark fruit with cinnamon and cherry, plus a subtle salty brine.
critics.finish: Medium-long with caramel, wood, salt and vanilla; called very unusual.
critics.summary: Batch 21 at 45% ABV; skeptic won over by the concept.

critics.nose: Floral notes with salted caramel, soft salt and light smoke.
critics.palate: Floral, citrus and light black pepper, then caramel with faint salt and smoke, dry oak.
critics.finish: Light dry oak with dominant caramel.
critics.summary: Batch 14; salt and smoke faded with time in glass; questioned the impact of sea aging.

facts.cask: Barrels matured aboard ocean-going ships

ks-jefferson-s-ocean-aged-at-sea-ksbw.notes: Ocean is released in numbered voyages/batches; critics reviewed batches 21 and 14, Kansas label voyage unknown. Producer page gives no proof; 45% ABV from Whiskey Jug.

critics.nose: Oak and cedar spice over deep caramel toffee, chocolate, cola, honeycomb and baking spice.
critics.palate: Dry and brash: oak, cedar, grass, butterscotch and bittersweet chocolate.
critics.finish: Medium length, smooth, with lingering dry spice.
critics.summary: Very Old bottling at 45.1% ABV; praised character and balance.

critics.nose: Popcorn, vanilla, raisin, butterscotch, peach and subtle ginger.
critics.palate: Chewy; hickory-smoked oak with salted butter, toffee, sweet corn, caramel and fruitcake spice.
critics.finish: Buttery popcorn, cinnamon and hot ginger building to a long peppery end.
critics.summary: Sampled 2014; 45.1% ABV bottling.

critics.nose: Deep caramel, vanilla, grassy rye spice and dark fruit.
critics.palate: Viscous and fruity: orange peel, floral vanilla, deep toffee.
critics.finish: Long and warming with caramel-dipped orange and white pepper.
critics.summary: 90.2-proof Very Old; a clear step up from Very Small Batch.

ks-jefferson-s-reserve-ksbw.notes: Kansas label (90 proof) matches the older 90.2-proof 'Very Old' Reserve. Current producer page describes a reformulated 8-year, 96-proof Reserve, so its notes were not used. Age claims vary (Difford's lists 12-17 yrs) so left null.

producer.nose: Balanced oak with fruit and dried apricot.
producer.palate: Sweet start, then white pepper spice from the high-rye recipe, with caramel and fruit.
producer.summary: Retailer (Seelbach's) product description, likely producer copy but not explicitly attributed; describes blending younger and older barrels.

critics.nose: Creamy caramel, light vanilla and oak with developing rye spice.
critics.palate: Heavy rye spice, green peppercorn, aged oak and vanilla.
critics.finish: Dry oak and leather with lingering woody rye spice.
critics.summary: Close to over-spiced but pleases spice lovers; competitive at $45. Rating not clearly captured.

critics.nose: Heavy rye spice, cinnamon, brown sugar, raisin-brandy, pine and apple cider.
critics.palate: Cinnamon candy spice with molasses cookie and baked apple; oak subtle.
critics.finish: Allspice, clove, citrus, tobacco and oak tannin held together by molasses.
critics.summary: Good entry point to the brand.

facts.region: Distilled in Indiana; Smoke Wagon is a Nevada brand

ks-smoke-wagon-small-batch-straight-bour.notes: Producer notes are retailer-relayed and unattributed.

producer.summary: Retailer (Seelbach's) description attributed to Smoke Wagon: rich and sweet with a very thick mouthfeel, likened to milk and cookies; proof cited around 115-116.

critics.nose: Floral and fruity: carnation, jammy cherry/raspberry, vanilla, cereal, noticeable ethanol.
critics.palate: Cinnamon, butterscotch, stewed apple and oak, moving to caramelized fruit and malt.
critics.finish: Long, creamy and chocolatey with lingering brown sugar.
critics.summary: August 2021 release; impressive complexity and integrated oak.

critics.nose: Caramel with an herbal edge, licorice, vanilla, candied pineapple, baked apple, oak, cinnamon, clove.
critics.palate: Caramel with earthy/herbal twist, vanilla, dried orange peel, baked apple, oak and spice.
critics.finish: Roasted oak, honey, vanilla cream, licorice, apple and pear.
critics.summary: Batch 14 at 57.1% ABV; rated 'Top Shelf' (top category).

facts.cask: Uncut, unfiltered

ks-smoke-wagon-uncut-unfiltered-straight.notes: Batch-strength product; Kansas label is 116.4 proof but reviewed batches were 57.1% ABV and a 2021 release in a 110-120 proof range. Producer description retailer-relayed.

producer.nose: Candied apple and smoked cherry wood.
producer.palate: Acidic and zesty, with orange curacao and candied ginger.
producer.finish: Coats the tongue and throat with a warming sensation.
producer.summary: Barrell's official notes as relayed by One More Dram's launch article (press release).

critics.nose: Crisp leaves, nectarine, caramel sauce, coffee cake, cinnamon.
critics.palate: Peach, spiced syrup, oak, rye spice, creamy vanilla; creamy mouthfeel.
critics.finish: Rye spice, leather, dry oak, baking spice, hint of tobacco leaf.
critics.summary: Strong blending; finish less memorable; worth the $85.

critics.nose: Green apple with caramel, tropical fruit, white pepper, chili powder and floral notes.
critics.palate: Caramel, butterscotch, maple, praline, then cooked apple, cherry, orange marmalade, milk chocolate, coffee and toffee.
critics.summary: Accessible yet deep for both casual and seasoned drinkers.

facts.age: Blend of 8-15 year bourbons (Indiana 8/11/12, Kentucky 10, Tennessee 13/14/15)

ks-barrell-bourbon-cask-strength-a-blend.notes: Exact batch match. Producer notes press-release relayed (Barrell shop page 404).

critics.nose: Sweet caramel, vanilla and toffee layered with nutmeg and oak.
critics.palate: Creamy, with honey and orange sweetness, spice and seasoned oak.
critics.finish: Heat spike, mild dryness, trailing caramel and spice with subtle smoke.
critics.summary: Easy-to-enjoy crowd-pleaser at its price.

critics.nose: Peanut, banana bread, hazelnut and sweet earthiness.
critics.palate: More rye-led than typical Wild Turkey; honey and milk chocolate with an odd savory sweetness.
critics.finish: Banana and milk chocolate with oak dryness and citrus.
critics.summary: Not a favorite but well put together.

facts.cask: Filtered through American white oak charcoal then Texas mesquite charcoal

ks-wild-turkey-longbranch-ksbw.notes: No producer notes: Wild Turkey Longbranch product page 404.

critics.nose: Candy corn, caramel, vanilla frosting, lemon zest, toasted oak, clove, rye spice, black cherry.
critics.palate: Caramel, vanilla, seasoned oak, graham cracker, light tobacco, black pepper, orange chocolate.
critics.finish: Rye spice and peppery oak with cinnamon, brown sugar, nutmeg and slight bitterness.
critics.summary: Better than standard 101, though the price bump may not justify it for everyone.

critics.nose: Dark roasted caramel, toasted vanilla, roasted oak, cinnamon, clove, dried grass, nuts.
critics.palate: Roasted caramel and vanilla, oak, cinnamon, nutmeg, cocoa, licorice, apple and orange.
critics.finish: Oak, coffee grounds, cinnamon, clove, burnt caramel and vanilla.
critics.summary: Export (Japan) bottling at 50.5% ABV; rated 'Mid shelf+'.

ks-wild-turkey-aged-8-years-ksbw.notes: Breaking Bourbon says the 8-year 101 became a US line extension after being export-only; Whiskey Shelf reviewed a Japan bottling. No producer page found (404).

critics.nose: Brown sugar, pralines, new leather, apricot, pepper and young creamed corn.
critics.palate: Caramel, brulee sugar, orange peel, cinnamon, lumber, peanut brittle, black pepper.
critics.finish: Medium length with vanilla wafer and ripe tangerine.
critics.summary: Graded A-.

critics.nose: Caramel, vanilla and pepper over roasted peanut, honeyed nougat and jalapeno cornbread.
critics.palate: Echoes the nose plus black pepper, vanilla cream, mint and circus peanut.
critics.finish: Medium-length, spicy and sweet.
critics.summary: Solid youthful everyday bourbon for sipping or mixing; Gold Medal.

facts.age: NAS; blend of 4-year in-house and 7-year sourced bourbon (per 2019 review)
facts.mash_bill: Limestone Branch distillate blended with sourced Kentucky bourbon

ks-yellowstone-select-ksbw.notes: Producer site had no product notes. Drinkhacker's age breakdown is from 2019 and may have changed.

ks-hardin-s-creek-ksbw-low-distillation.notes: Could not identify a Hardin's Creek 'Low Distillation' release at 109 proof; the Beam current-releases page lists only the 110-proof 2025 Warehouse Series, and hardinscreek.com was unreachable. Possibly a newer release not yet indexed.

producer.nose: Oak, vanilla and subtle spice.
producer.palate: Caramel and honey with a hint of agave from the tequila barrels.
producer.finish: Long and warm, with spice and sweetness.
producer.summary: Notes presented as producer notes on the Wooden Cork retailer page (retailer-relayed). Master Distiller John Rempe described the anejo-cask finish as bringing bourbon full circle (quoted via Whiskeyfellow).

critics.nose: Earthy oak, smoky vanilla, cherry, toffee, leather and agave.
critics.palate: Creamy; smoky vanilla, lime zest, nutmeg, dark chocolate, black cherry, oak spice, tobacco, agave.
critics.finish: Long; oak spice, nutmeg, dark chocolate, black cherry, old leather, cinnamon.
critics.summary: 'Bottle' rating; tequila notes complement rather than dominate.

critics.nose: Pine and oak with lemon zest, some bitterness and heat.
critics.palate: Toffee and nougat with pine and oak.
critics.finish: Astringent at first, returning to toffee.
critics.summary: Letter grade B-; bitter streaks detract, though not bad.

critics.nose: Bright, sweet and delicate: soft grain, waffle cone, lemon peel, subtle agave.
critics.palate: Vanilla, butterscotch, agave, orange peel, clove, barrel char.
critics.finish: Long; raisin, macadamia, agave, citrus peel, grapefruit, char.
critics.summary: Called it a lovely bourbon with a well-integrated tequila-cask finish; numeric score and scale ambiguous in fetch, so omitted.

facts.age: Blend of 14-year and 7-year traditional bourbon with 10-year wheated bourbon
facts.cask: Finished in anejo tequila barrels

ks-blood-oath-pact-11-ksbw.notes: Producer tasting notes are retailer-relayed only.

producer.summary: Distillery describes it as elegant, fruit-driven and sweet, good neat, on the rocks or in cocktails; relayed by the Seelbach's retailer page.

critics.nose: Caramel, vanilla, oak and pear; traditional bourbon aroma.
critics.palate: Oak, pepper, trail mix, banana; thin and quite oaky.
critics.finish: Oak and pepper, dry.
critics.summary: Surprisingly oaky for 4 years; expected more from the blended mashbills.

facts.mash_bill: Blend of 60% corn/20% rye/20% malted barley and 51% corn/20% rye/20% malted barley/9% wheat

ks-starlight-distillery-carl-t-bourbon-w.notes: Producer statement is a brief retailer-relayed summary only (no nose/palate/finish).

producer.summary: Producer notes quoted by The Whiskey Shelf: bold and spicy at first, mellowing to sweet caramel and maple, likened to an oatmeal raisin cookie.

critics.nose: Fruit-forward: cherry candy, orange jelly, raisin, light brown sugar, subtle oak.
critics.palate: Light-bodied; cherry, orange, lemon, vanilla, brown sugar, cinnamon, clove, leather.
critics.finish: Slightly bitter citrus and dry oak with cherry, vanilla and creme brulee.
critics.summary: Versatile and approachable.

critics.nose: Molasses-like sweetness turning to grass, charcoal and nutmeg.
critics.palate: Smooth caramel with spicier notes.
critics.summary: Balanced; somewhat pricey but worth trying.

critics.nose: Shy; grassy, nougat caramel, vanilla, pine, maple.
critics.palate: Brown sugar, dried apricot, vanilla, roasted oak with a grainy, cracker-like harshness.
critics.finish: Honey, fennel, roasted oak, dried apricot; dry and spicy.
critics.summary: Rated 'Mid Shelf'; disappointed, drinks like a cheaper bottle.

facts.cask: Maple charcoal filtered (Lincoln County Process); charred new American oak

ks-uncle-nearest-1856-aged-whiskey.notes: Producer notes are second-hand (quoted in a review); Uncle Nearest product page 404.

producer.summary: Jack Daniel's says it is bottled straight from the barrel at full proof (125-140), with intensified vanilla and toasted oak; robust but not overpowering.

critics.nose: Maple sugar candy and banana over burnt wood; inviting smoke.
critics.palate: Chocolatey caramel, burnt wood, pipe tobacco, banana, nuts; drinks lower than its proof.
critics.finish: Bold, spicy, near-tannic heat that fades to burnt wood and maple.
critics.summary: Barrel at 130.6 proof; recommended despite barrel variation. Rating not clearly captured.

critics.nose: Banana bread, toasted marshmallow, deep caramel, faint salted almond.
critics.palate: Praline pecan, overripe banana, buttery biscuit; little heat.
critics.finish: Oak tannin, dry leather, dark chocolate and charred marshmallow.
critics.summary: Rural Inn store pick at 135.7 proof.

facts.cask: Single barrel, barrel proof (125-140 proof range)

ks-jack-daniel-s-single-barrel-barrel-pr.notes: Single-barrel product, so each barrel differs; Kansas label is 129 proof, reviews are of 130.6- and 135.7-proof barrels. Mash bill omitted (sources disagree on rye vs barley split).

critics.nose: Fresh and vegetal with mint and oak.
critics.palate: Grain and earth, then raisin, cinnamon and caramel.
critics.finish: Smooth and mellow.
critics.summary: Enjoyable for all experience levels.

critics.nose: Banana nut bread, caramel, maple, light cinnamon and vanilla.
critics.palate: Brown sugar and maple, nuttiness, banana and vanilla; little oak.
critics.finish: Graham cracker, vanilla, brown sugar; moderate length, minimal burn.
critics.summary: Big step up from the 80-proof standard but not exciting.

facts.cask: Bottled in bond

ks-jack-daniel-s-bonded-tennessee-whiske.notes: No producer notes (Jack Daniel's Bonded page 404).

critics.nose: Clean and crisp: green apple, honey, cinnamon, caramel, corn, orchard fruit, char.
critics.palate: Honey, apple, corn, apricot, rye spice, caramel, wood, pine-mint.
critics.finish: Medium; caramel, honey, spice, wood and mint.
critics.summary: Praised drinkability and balance; a repeat purchase for the reviewer.

critics.nose: Banana with vanilla, like bananas foster.
critics.palate: Weightier than Jack Daniel's, light maple-syrup feel with apple and oak spice.
critics.finish: Slightly bitter on ice, with fruit and oak spice.
critics.summary: Good in cocktails, especially a mule.

ks-george-dickel-tennessee-sour-mash-whi.notes: No producer notes found. Whiskey Jug score omitted (scale unclear in fetch).

producer.nose: Fresh cherries, almonds and cedar.
producer.summary: Official notes relayed by BroBible: fruit-forward with heavy nut character; charcoal mellowing gives a creamy mouthfeel.

critics.nose: Dried corn, brown sugar, oak, caramel, baking spice, leather, dried cherry, vanilla.
critics.palate: Mirrors the nose: dried corn, caramel, oak, cinnamon, leather, tart cherry.
critics.finish: Long; dried corn, oak, caramel and spice.
critics.summary: Summed up as spiced caramel corn; recommended neat or in a Manhattan. Letter-grade style rating (B+ range), numeric score omitted.

facts.cask: Bottled in bond; distilled Fall 2008

ks-george-dickel-13-year-tennessee-whisk.notes: Whiskey Wash review of Fall 2008 skipped: it covered the earlier 11-year release. Whiskey Shelf 13-year review was a 2005 distillation, skipped. Producer notes relayed by BroBible.

critics.nose: Crisp apple, white peach, cedar, vanilla, light syrup.
critics.palate: Caramel and brown sugar, baking and rye spice, vanilla, oak.
critics.finish: Vanilla, oak, leather, white peppercorn, brown sugar.
critics.summary: Well-rounded Washington bourbon that holds up to Kentucky at 90 proof. Rating not clearly captured.

critics.nose: Grain, hay, lactic sourness, cashew, lemon, puff pastry.
critics.palate: Light and gently sweet: honey, custard, nutmeg, baked apple.
critics.finish: Sweet and chewy.

facts.age: NAS (5 years per company, via Breaking Bourbon)

ks-woodinville-straight-bourbon-whiskey.notes: No producer notes: Woodinville shop lists finished variants; plain straight bourbon page not found.

producer.summary: Producer page: rich texture with sticky baked plum and chocolate-covered cherry; finished six months in Douro Valley port barrels.

critics.nose: Vanilla, blueberry, raspberry, seasoned oak.
critics.palate: Raspberry, grape, caramel, dark chocolate; good mouthfeel.
critics.finish: Plum, grape, seasoned oak, light leather, dry port aftertaste.
critics.summary: Sweet, fruit-forward daily drinker; dry winey finish holds it back.

facts.cask: Finished about six months in port barrels from the Douro Valley

ks-woodinville-bourbon-whiskey-port-cask.notes: Producer gives a descriptive summary rather than split nose/palate/finish.

producer.nose: Honey-drizzled apple slices, verbena, fresh-cut grass, saddle leather and cinnamon.
producer.palate: Tart orange and lemon candy, pound cake, sugar cookie, smoky baking spice, honeysuckle.
producer.finish: Long; smoky tobacco turning to caramel apple with walnut and cinnamon.
producer.summary: Official Garrison Brothers notes; grain-to-glass Texas bourbon aged in intense heat.

critics.nose: Raw grainy corn, caramel, sweet tea, cigar wrapper, leather, maple.
critics.palate: Chocolate, leather, charred oak, butterscotch pudding, honey candy; little baking spice.
critics.finish: More oak; chocolate, leather, caramel, honey, coffee liqueur.
critics.summary: Worth trying once for wheated-bourbon fans.

critics.nose: Maple gingerbread, toasted sesame, vanilla, toasted oak, marzipan, herbs.
critics.palate: Butterscotch, spiced pine, maple, chocolate-chip pancake, dried mango.
critics.finish: Slightly tannic and oaky in a flavorful way.
critics.summary: 3-year-old at 94 proof; Gold Medal (archived 2023 review).

ks-garrison-brothers-small-batch-texas-s.notes: Mash percentages and age come from critics, not the producer page.

critics.nose: Raisin and oak, cereal, faint cinnamon and baking spice, char.
critics.palate: Baking spice and rye warmth, coffee and leather bitterness, char; creamy.
critics.finish: Creamy with straw.
critics.summary: Standout in the Balcones range; drinks rye-like.

critics.nose: Sawdust and oak spice, then honey, vanilla, toffee, canned peach, apricot jam, cocoa.
critics.palate: Spicy charred oak and toasted nuts, then vanilla, creamed corn, cooked apricot, stewed apple.
critics.finish: Long, spicy and drying; clove, cocoa, sandalwood.
critics.summary: Called it delicious with great structure.
