producer.summary: Notes from retailer Flaviar's listing (attribution to brand not stated). Made by Romulo Sanchez Parada in Candelaria Yegole, Oaxaca, at a family palenque dating to 1870.

critics.nose: Seemingly endless clay, wet earth, charred cinnamon and sweet spicy smoke.
critics.palate: Blistered pineapple, bright acidity, fresh aloe and hay; piquant texture.
critics.finish: Delicate white florals; slightly sweet and earthy.
critics.summary: Reviewed bottle at 48.5% ABV, distilled August 2019.

critics.nose: Lily of the valley, grapefruit rind and green pepper.
critics.summary: Surprisingly floral and delicate for the style; profile listed as fruity. Listing shows 48% ABV.

facts.mash_bill: Espadin (A. angustifolia), 7-10 years old; tahona crushed, open-air fermentation with natural yeasts up to 12 days
facts.cask: In-ground oven up to 5 days; double distilled in small copper pot stills
facts.region: Oaxaca, Mexico (Mezcalistas gives Zoquitlan; Flaviar gives Candelaria Yegole)

ks-mezcal-rey-campero-joven-espadin-vice.notes: Label names 'Vicente', but every source found credits Romulo Sanchez Parada; could be a different lot/mezcalero not covered by these sources. ABV varies by lot (48 vs 48.5%); Mezcalistas lot matches 48.5%.

producer.summary: No producer notes found. Retailer Wooden Cork (own description) cites earthy roasted agave, layered smoke and minerality with a long finish; Mission Liquor notes the Tapanala spring water used for fermentation and proofing.

critics.nose: Wet stone over cooked agave with green herbs.
critics.palate: Mid-weight and clean, with a distinct mineral signature from the spring water.
critics.finish: Mineral, faintly sweet and long.
critics.summary: Reviewed at 43% ABV.

facts.mash_bill: Espadin (A. angustifolia); mezcaleros Adan and Joelito Barriga; proofed with local Sierra Sur spring water
facts.cask: Tahona mill, copper still

ks-vago-el-manantial-by-hijos-de-barriga.notes: Sources list 43% ABV vs 42% on the Kansas label (batch variation likely). Mezcal Report's editorial standing is unclear. Community reviews on mezcalreviews.com not used as critics.

critics.nose: Grilled ripe pineapple, smoked banana peel, toffee, cardamom and peanut brittle.
critics.palate: Velvety yet crisp and dry, light-to-medium body; dunder, umami smoke, grilled fruit, roasted spiced nuts, cedar shavings.
critics.finish: Tingling medium length with smoke and spice.
critics.summary: Gold medal; vibrant, tropical-fruit-forward Jamaican rum. Reviewed at 43% ABV under the Planteray name.

critics.nose: Pungent buttery pastry, vanilla, baked banana, pineapple, zesty orange and faint smoke.
critics.palate: Full-bodied and dry; ripe pear amid tropical fruit with peppery pot-still spice.
critics.finish: Pot-still spice with mellowing vanilla, buttery pastry and a little smoke.
critics.summary: Big, characterful rum. Sampled 2020 (Plantation label), 43% ABV.

critics.nose: Sweet and oaky with cognac influence; pineapple juice, black banana, spicy oak, lemon zest.
critics.palate: Spicy (white pepper, ginger, allspice) with fruit and toffee, but thin mid-palate.
critics.finish: Woody and fairly short.
critics.summary: Found it too soft and polite, lacking typical Jamaican pot-still funk. Reviewed Plantation-labelled 43% bottling.

facts.age: No age statement; 1-3 years in ex-bourbon casks in Jamaica plus about 1 year in
facts.mash_bill: 100% pot still Jamaican rum from Long Pond and Clarendon distilleries; 0 g/L dosage (per Fat Rum Pirate)
facts.cask: Ex-bourbon American oak, finished in cognac-seasoned French oak

ks-planteray-xaymaca-special-dry-pot-sti.notes: Producer site (planteray.com) unreachable; no producer notes. Two of three critics reviewed the pre-2023 'Plantation' label of the same 43% expression.

producer.nose: Intense, precise coffee, orange, plum, jam and truffle.
producer.palate: Caramel cream, chocolate and vanilla, then cinnamon, raisin, nutmeg, oak and molasses with smoky touches.
producer.finish: Long, with dark chocolate, clove and caramel.
producer.summary: Maison Ferrand/Plantation notes as relayed by retailer InternetWines.com. Blend developed by Alexandre Gabriel with a group of rum experts; name stands for Old Fashioned Traditional Dark.

critics.nose: Pungent burnt currant, caramelised brown sugar, orange zest, vanilla, coffee, chocolate, overripe banana.
critics.palate: Spicy and fruity: plum, currant, molasses, vanilla, dry oak, charcoal, warming baking spice and black pepper.
critics.finish: Clove, cinnamon, black pepper and burnt currant.
critics.summary: Powerful and characterful. Sampled 2017 (Plantation label) at 69%.

critics.nose: Heavy molasses with cane/grassy notes and earthy funk; cinnamon, nutmeg, allspice, tropical fruit, a touch of brine.
critics.palate: Molasses and baking spice against fruit, with brine, citrus and slight Jamaican funk.
critics.finish: Drying with only a touch of burn.
critics.summary: Navy-style overproof; value rated 9/10. Reviewed at 138 proof.

facts.mash_bill: Molasses rums from Barbados (WIRD), Jamaica (Long Pond) and Guyana (Demerara Distillers); 0 g/L dosage

ks-planteray-o-f-t-d-overproof-rum.notes: Producer notes are retailer-relayed (planteray.com unreachable). Difford's sampled the earlier Plantation-labelled release of the same 69% blend.

producer.summary: No producer notes fetched. Retailer InternetWines.com relays brand framing: a tribute to historic Caribbean rums, with Barbados giving richness, Trinidad finesse and Jamaica structure.

critics.nose: Tropical fruit, vanilla, minerals and cardamom.
critics.palate: Lush, fruity and raw, with cane, spice, vanilla, grass and mineral notes.
critics.summary: Holds its presence in cocktails without dominating; value rated 9/10. Reviewed at 41.2%.

critics.nose: Bright and fruity: coconut meat, confectioners sugar, sawdust, mango.
critics.palate: Good mouthfeel; honey, coconut, lightly lactic, lots of caramel, restrained funk.
critics.finish: Short but flavorful: coconut cream, lemon, mango, pencil shavings, honey.
critics.summary: Cocktail workhorse that also works neat or on ice. Reviewed Plantation-labelled bottle at 41.2%.

facts.age: Blend: Barbados unaged, Trinidad 2-3 years, Jamaica unaged with a small 10-year
facts.mash_bill: Molasses rums from Barbados, Trinidad and Jamaica; twin column, column and pot stills

ks-planteray-3-stars-rum.notes: No producer tasting notes (planteray.com unreachable). Daily Pour reviewed the earlier Plantation label of the same 41.2% blend.

producer.nose: Toffee, orange peel and licorice.
producer.palate: Complex and balanced, with oak and vanilla.
producer.finish: Long-lasting, carried by the oak and vanilla notes.
producer.summary: Amber; producer stresses its signature smoothness and balance as a super-premium sipping rum.

critics.palate: Rich, velvety and full-bodied; caramelized toffee, orange zest, cinnamon-dusted cocoa.
critics.finish: Lingering hint of cinnamon and cocoa.
critics.summary: Smooth, sweet-profile sipper; reviewed at 40%.

critics.palate: Bold, dark, fruity and full-bodied.
critics.summary: A rum that really tastes of something; profile listed as sweet and rich.

critics.nose: Very sweet: orange, grape, raisin, chocolate and a syrupy note.
critics.palate: Smooth and viscous; vanilla, fudge/toffee sauce, slightly bitter cocoa, liqueur-like.
critics.finish: Fairly short with some oak.
critics.summary: Enjoyable and easy but reviewer suspects added sugar/liqueur, which lowered the rating.

facts.age: No age statement; blend of rums up to 12 years (per Distiller)
facts.mash_bill: Molasses and sugarcane honey; copper pot-still rums (per Distiller)
facts.cask: Ex-bourbon barrels (per Distiller)

ks-diplomatico-reserva-exclusiva-rum.notes: Producer page gives nose/palate only; finish line paraphrases its palate sentence. Age/still/cask facts from Distiller, not the producer.

producer.nose: Lush tropical fruit and spice with hints of honey and dark sugar.
producer.palate: Mellow and full-bodied, rich in fruit and spice.
producer.summary: Estery richness credited to wooden and metal Coffey stills.

critics.nose: Prunes, dates, banoffee pie and toffee apple, with hints of tar, coffee and vanilla.
critics.palate: Slightly sweet: mocha, dark chocolate, sherry trifle, cooked apple and cinnamon.
critics.finish: Drier; dark chocolate and espresso with lingering spice.
critics.summary: Sampled 2010 at 40% ABV.

critics.nose: Sweet raisin, plum and caramel; lighter and fruitier than typical Demerara, some strawberry.
critics.palate: Raisin and caramel, then milk chocolate and berries; a little underpowered, dries quickly.
critics.finish: Short; oak and white pepper with an astringent aftertaste.
critics.summary: Good but only just; notes additive level cut to about 6 g/L from 39 g/L in 2014. Reviewed at 40%.

facts.mash_bill: Molasses rum blended from Enmore wooden Coffey, Diamond metal Coffey and Port Mourant double wooden pot stills (per Fat Rum Pirate)

ks-el-dorado-aged-12-years-finest-demera.notes: Difford's tasting is old (2010) and may predate the reduced-sugar reformulation noted by Fat Rum Pirate. Still lists differ slightly between sources.

producer.nose: Full nose of dark coffee, candied orange, almond, dark chocolate, pepper and vanilla.
producer.palate: Grilled tropical fruit with smooth oaky spice; moderately full-bodied.
producer.finish: Earthy, peat-like, attributed to the Port Mourant still.
producer.summary: Blend from EHP wooden Coffey, metal Coffey, Port Mourant double wooden pot and Versailles single wooden pot stills.

critics.nose: Very sweet at first: apple, banana and rum-soaked raisins.
critics.palate: Sweet stone fruit, then oak with slightly bitter dark chocolate and cocoa; coating and intense.
critics.finish: Long, spicy and fruity with oak and bittersweetness.
critics.summary: Very high praise (top star rating); notes it uses different still components than the 12, not just longer aging. Reviewed at 43% (UK).

critics.source: The Whisky Exchange (Stuart P, retailer staff)
critics.nose: Christmas-cake character: candied peel, allspice, cinnamon, dried fruit, golden syrup.
critics.palate: Spicy dried fruit layered with honey, gingerbread and toasty oak.
critics.finish: Persistent, honeyed and spicy.
critics.summary: Retailer staff tasting note; 43% UK bottling, colouring listed.

facts.mash_bill: Molasses rum from EHP wooden Coffey, metal Coffey, Port Mourant and Versailles wooden pot stills

ks-el-dorado-aged-15-years-finest-demera.notes: ABV mismatch: Kansas record says 40% (80 proof) but both critic sources list 43%; facts.abv is the 43% from those sources (producer page gave no ABV). Fat Rum Pirate star score not recorded because the exact value was unclear.

producer.palate: Ripe banana and toasted almond.
producer.summary: Master blender (Allen Smith) notes as relayed in a Chilled Magazine release article (2016); nose described only in general terms. Limited to 3,000 bottles for Barbados' 50th independence anniversary.

critics.nose: Heavy barrel char, licorice and coffee bean, with dark chocolate and clove.
critics.palate: Dusky notes carry through neat; with water, wood, baking spice, sweet coffee, molasses cookie and ginger.
critics.summary: Graded A-. Reviewed at 126 proof.

critics.nose: Pronounced spicy oak with bourbon-cask influence; vanilla, creamy nuttiness, hint of banana, toffee and caramel.
critics.palate: Spicy and oaky, then toffee, caramel, chocolate, peach and banana.
critics.finish: Long, spicy and tingly.
critics.summary: A concentrated version of standard XO; can lean dry/oaky; best with a little water. Reviewed at 63%.

facts.mash_bill: Molasses; pot and column still blend (per Fat Rum Pirate)

ks-mount-gay-xo-cask-strength-limited-ed.notes: Sources describe the November 2016 limited release (3,000 bottles); if the Kansas registration is a later edition, details may differ. Producer notes are press-relayed; not listed on mountgayrum.com.

producer.nose: Toasted oak and butter balanced by dried fruit and spice.
producer.palate: Bold and aromatic: orange zest, black pepper, toasted vanilla and toffee.
producer.summary: Column and double-retort pot still rum, matured in ex-American whiskey casks and finished six months in heavily charred ex-bourbon casks.

critics.nose: Lighter, softer and more balanced; char and smoke with toffee/caramel and vanilla ice cream.
critics.palate: Icing sugar, banana, pineapple, green apple and gooseberry, then dry, slightly bourbon-like spice and char.
critics.finish: Good length; spicy, easy-going Barbadian mix of char, vanilla and soft fruit.
critics.summary: Reviewed the 2020 Double Cask reformulation (3-7 year blend, more pot still) at 43%.

facts.mash_bill: Molasses; traditional column and double retort pot stills
facts.cask: Ex-American whiskey casks, finished 6 months in heavily charred ex-bourbon casks

ks-mount-gay-black-barrel-double-cask-bl.notes: Producer page gives no ABV; 43% and 3-7 year age from The Whisky Exchange and Fat Rum Pirate.

producer.nose: Toasted oak, dried fruit and hazelnut, then dark cocoa, molasses, orange peel, vanilla and a hint of coffee.
producer.summary: Deep bronze with gold and mahogany glints; blended by Joy Spence from pot and column still rums, limestone-filtered water, no added flavours. Producer page labels the expression 'Rare Casks'.

critics.nose: Wood spice, tobacco, caramel, bitter orange zest, ripe banana, dried apricot and anise.
critics.palate: Caramelized vanilla, orange zest and oak spice, then hazelnut, dark chocolate, brown sugar and char.
critics.finish: Long; dried apricot and anise as oak tannins take over.
critics.summary: Mahogany color; reviewed at 43%.

critics.nose: Pineapple, coconut, banana and mango over brown sugar and toffee.
critics.palate: Vanilla, brown sugar and dark chocolate lead, with banana and pineapple behind.
critics.finish: Pineapple with restrained Jamaican funk.
critics.summary: Smooth and balanced mix of barrel character and tropical fruit. Reviewed at 43%.

facts.mash_bill: Jamaican molasses rum; pot and column still blend
facts.cask: Used bourbon barrels (per Got Rum?)

ks-appleton-estate-aged-12-years-rare-bl.notes: Kansas label says 'Rare Blend'; current producer and critic naming is 'Rare Casks' (same 12-year, 43% expression). Producer page gives appearance in place of a palate note.

producer.summary: Producer description relayed by retailer Berry Bros. & Rudd: overripe banana, mango, vanilla and red apple with nutmeg and cinnamon. Producer claims 8 tropical years equal almost 25 in a European climate.

critics.nose: Easy-going and tropical: vanilla pod, guava, ripe pineapple, pear, clove, cardamom, mint, tobacco, varnish and polish.
critics.palate: Spicier: charred oak, cocoa nibs, mint chocolate, peat-like smoke, pineapple juice, cinnamon, ginger, black pepper, lemon zest.
critics.finish: Long, with vanilla and fresh pineapple.
critics.summary: Score combines flavour, value and transparency subscores. Reviewed at 46%.

critics.nose: Ripe banana, tropical fruit, banana bread.
critics.palate: Banana, pineapple, banana bread, vanilla, caramelised apple, slight savouriness, light spice.
critics.finish: Savoury with a light vegetal note.
critics.summary: Good introduction to estery, funky Jamaican rum; strong daiquiri base. Reviewed at 46%.

facts.age: 8 years minimum, tropically aged in Jamaica
facts.mash_bill: Molasses; extended open-vat fermentation; OWH marque (per The Rum Barrel); pot still
facts.cask: Ex-bourbon casks

ks-hampden-estate-aged-8-years-rum.notes: Producer notes are a single retailer-relayed sentence (put in summary, not split into nose/palate).

producer.nose: Heady dried fruit, cocoa and green plantain.
producer.palate: Banana, pineapple and orange, then creme brulee, cacao and coffee with high-ester Jamaican funk.
producer.summary: Official notes via US importer Back Bar Project; appearance dark chocolate with deep copper flashes.

critics.nose: Chocolate, cola, banana, toasted sugar and oak with background fruit.
critics.palate: Oak and banana with orange, bubble gum, allspice and vanilla.
critics.finish: Moderate length, echoing chocolate and spice.
critics.summary: Neat 7.8, mixer 8.1; rated an incredible value. Notes no added sugar but added color. Reviewed at 54.5%.

facts.age: Light-ester rum aged 3 years blended with unaged higher-ester rum
facts.mash_bill: Estate molasses; 100% copper pot still (double retort per Rum Runner Labs)
facts.cask: Ex-bourbon casks (once-used per Difford's)

ks-worthy-park-109-jamaica-rum.notes: Difford's page had facts only, no tasting notes. Rum Runner Labs lists minimum age 0 (reflecting the unaged component).

producer.summary: Official description via US importer Skurnik: rich and unctuous, with grapefruit, caramelized orange, toffee, nougat, butterscotch and brown butter over leather, tobacco and tropical fruit. Oldest Foursquare release; final Exceptional Cask Series bottling (Mark XXXI).

critics.nose: Oak-driven rather than fruity; oak, leather and tobacco lead.
critics.palate: Dark toffee and orange peel, then roasted hazelnut and cracked pepper, with clove and cinnamon.
critics.finish: Long, dry and clean: leathery tobacco, dark cocoa, dry blackberry.
critics.summary: Top rating; a refined conclusion to the ECS series. Reviewed at 57%.

facts.mash_bill: Molasses; blend of double-retort copper pot still and twin Coffey column still rum; no added sugar or colouring
facts.cask: Ex-bourbon barrels

ks-foursquare-epliogue-single-blended-ru.notes: Kansas name misspells 'Epilogue'. Rumporter (2026) covered the release and reports an IWSC 2026 gold but gave no tasting notes.

producer.nose: Soft and sweet: caramel, vanilla, cacao and butterscotch, then sherried dried fruit.
producer.palate: Complex, generous and full-bodied; dried fruit, oak, spice and coffee with cinnamon and ginger.
producer.finish: Intricate; honeyed butterscotch, spiced oak and dried fruit.
producer.summary: Solera blend of rums aged 6 to 23 years in casks that held American whiskey, sherry and Pedro Ximenez.

critics.palate: Roasted coffee, butterscotch, vanilla and dark chocolate, refreshed by citrus, apricot, herbal notes, nutmeg and ginger.
critics.finish: Long: caramel, pipe tobacco, cedar and roasted nuts.
critics.summary: One of the most pleasurable dark rums to sip neat; profile listed as sweet and rich.

critics.nose: Sweet brown sugar like caramel/toffee sauce, with oak and cocoa.
critics.palate: Surprisingly dry and oaky; cocoa and tropical fruit develop; very smooth.
critics.finish: Smooth with little burn or aftertaste.
critics.summary: Complex, works neat or mixed. Reviewed at 40%.

facts.age: No age statement; solera blend of rums aged 6-23 years
facts.mash_bill: Virgin sugarcane honey; pineapple-derived yeast; copper-lined column still (per Distiller)
facts.cask: Ex-American whiskey, sherry and Pedro Ximenez casks (solera)

ks-ron-zacapa-centerario-23-year-old-rum.notes: Kansas record misspells 'Centenario' and duplicates the name in the producer field. '23' is a solera designation, not a true 23-year age statement.

producer.nose: Red fruit, honey and toasted nuts.
producer.palate: Wood, vanilla and baked apple.
producer.summary: Reddish amber single-estate rum aged in bourbon barrels at the foot of an active volcano; no additives.

critics.nose: Orange zest and vanilla, then caramel, honey, light molasses, cooked apple, allspice, nutmeg and a faint floral lift.
critics.palate: Creamy and layered: caramel, nougat, nutmeg, allspice and orange peel.
critics.finish: Medium-long: honey, dried orange peel, gentle spice, oak, roasted almond, vanilla, tobacco leaf.
critics.summary: Elegant and approachable. Reviewed at 40% (2025 pricing).

critics.nose: Gentle molasses, brown sugar, honey, almond, cinnamon and light florals with vanilla, leather and smoke.
critics.palate: Caramel, bonbons, light molasses, honey, white chocolate, orange peel and nougat.
critics.finish: Brief and simple.
critics.summary: Found it unremarkable next to El Dorado 12 and Appleton 12. Reviewed at 40%.

facts.cask: Ex-bourbon barrels

ks-flor-de-cana-aged-12-years-rum.notes: Producer page combines palate and finish in one sentence; ABV not on producer page (40% from critics). Wine Enthusiast page failed (redirect loop).

producer.summary: No producer tasting notes found; The Rum Howler quotes only label marketing from the house of Martin Doorly.

critics.nose: Oak spice, caramel, maple, banana, orange peel, dark tobacco, marmalade and apricot jam; subtle sherry.
critics.palate: Sweet fruit and caramel, then tobacco and tart oak; apricot brandy, marzipan, walnut, light smokiness.
critics.finish: Peppery spice with caramel, orange zest and a last wisp of smoke.
critics.summary: Silver-level; recommended for sipping or quality mixing. Reviewed at 40%.

critics.nose: Subtle tropical fruit and vanilla with sweet toffee.
critics.palate: Sweet toffee, banana, orange and citrus; smooth, slightly dry Bajan style.
critics.finish: Long and spicy with a hint of oak.
critics.summary: Reviewed at 40%.

facts.age: No age statement; blend reportedly 6-10 or 6-12 years (sources differ)
facts.cask: American oak, then finished in oloroso sherry casks

ks-doorly-s-xo-rum-fine-old-barbados-rum.notes: ABV mismatch: Kansas label is 43% but both critics reviewed 40% bottlings (facts reflect sources); may be a different market strength. No producer notes.

producer.nose: Heavy wood and vanilla with dried fruit and coconut, opening toward grilled tropical fruit.
producer.palate: Lush and spicy (winter baking spice), turning to toasted wood and vanilla with hints of dried and exotic fruit.
producer.summary: Robust, spirited agricole pitched as an entry to premium rum; suggested neat or in an Old Fashioned or Manhattan. Notes from Rhum J.M USA site.

critics.nose: Richer than expected: maple, caramel, leathery oak, vanilla, almond, cinnamon, wood sap.
critics.palate: Light caramel and maple with leathery oak, herbal grassiness, vanilla, baking spice and praline.
critics.finish: Fairly short; leathery, grassy, butterscotch, mild heat.
critics.summary: Silver-level; pleasant but not highly complex. Reviewed at 43%.

critics.nose: Clean: apple, maple syrup, smoke, toasted sugar, oak, dried fruit.
critics.palate: Sweet with ginger, caramel, apple and late grassiness.
critics.finish: Moderately strong; nutmeg-led baking spice and orange peel.
critics.summary: Neat 7.2, mixer 8.3; strong agricole entry point that shines in cocktails. Reviewed at 43%.

critics.nose: Cola and Madeira over vanilla and brown sugar.
critics.palate: Wine-forward with red berry, then smoldering, ashy molasses.
critics.finish: Raisin-sweet but drying, with lingering molasses.
critics.summary: Graded A-. Reviewed at 86 proof.

facts.mash_bill: AOC Martinique rhum agricole from estate-grown fresh cane juice; single column still (per Rum Runner Labs)
facts.cask: Toasted new American oak

ks-rhum-j-m-v-o-rum.notes: Producer page gives nose and palate only. Region detail (Macouba) from The Rum Howler.

critics.nose: Juniper lightened by musky rose, with sweet orange, lime zest and elderflower.
critics.palate: Classic juniper, coriander and angelica, with candy-like orange and lime mid-palate.
critics.finish: Long and astringent: soaked rose petal, lime, cucumber, Earl Grey and some bitterness.
critics.summary: Reviewed the 44% US bottling.

critics.nose: Floral and fresh: musky rose, perfumed elderflower, cucumber; subtle juniper, orange zest.
critics.palate: Light and delicate; cucumber juice, frangipani, white tea tannin, mild coriander, white pepper, angelica.
critics.finish: Medium; cooling mint and cucumber fading to juniper, potpourri, angelica.
critics.summary: Elegant and gentle; best in martinis or G&Ts. Reviewed at 44%.

facts.mash_bill: Botanicals: angelica, caraway, chamomile, coriander, cubeb, elderflower, juniper, lemon, orange, orris, yarrow; plus rose and cucumber essences added after dist
facts.cask: Carter-head still and pot (Bennett) still distillates blended

ks-hendrick-s-gin.notes: Producer site behind age gate; no producer notes. facts.cask holds still info (gin is unaged); botanical list from The Gin Is In.

producer.nose: Ripe fruit, candied orange and light juniper; apple, watermelon, mango, peach, dried banana, sugared almond and light toasted oak.
producer.palate: Creamy and viscous; fresh fruit with vanilla ice cream and toasted oak, gentle earthy spice.
producer.finish: Lingering tropical fruit; oaky vanilla fades to grilled pineapple and mango with coriander, candied orange, juniper and cassia.
producer.summary: Bruichladdich gin with 22 hand-foraged Islay botanicals, matured at least 3 years in oak.

critics.nose: Earthy, peppery and woody with cardamom, florals and orange slices.
critics.palate: Candied orange, toffee, pepper, spicy oak and vanilla with subtle juniper.
critics.finish: Subtle mixed spice and pepper.
critics.summary: Reviewed alongside the younger Cask Rested gin; Cask Aged is the 3+ year, 46% release.

critics.palate: Prominent wood with vanilla sweetness and a distinctive grilled pineapple note.
critics.summary: Well balanced between gin and brown spirit. Reviewed at 46%.

facts.cask: Blend of oak casks incl. bourbon, Amarone, Sauternes, Pauillac, rum and St. Emilion

ks-the-botanist-islay-cask-aged-gin.notes: Distinct from the Islay Cask Rested gin (6+ months). Wine Enthusiast page failed (redirect loop).

producer.summary: Producer describes pure juniper scent, tangy crisp citrus, sweet floral aroma, a hint of peppery spice, subtle bitter fruit and a racy finish. Batch-distilled, unfiltered, 47 botanicals (several from the Black Forest such as spruce, lingonberries, sloe and elderflower), rested in earthenware.

critics.palate: Forest fruits with wildflower and island spice notes; juniper present but not dominant.
critics.finish: Balanced, long and rich.
critics.summary: Calls it an exquisite gin that pushes the limits of flavor in the category.

critics.nose: Prominent juniper with intense herbal notes: dried rosemary, cloves, dried mushroom.
critics.palate: Fresh rosemary, evergreen, black pepper and a big forest-floor, earthy, campfire-ember element; fruit (blueberry, orange, apple, peach) emerges late.
critics.finish: Sweet, fruity, slightly tart; very easy drinking.
critics.summary: Graded A- (letter grade). Calls it bizarre, fun and wholly unique. Reviewed at 94 proof.

critics.nose: Very complex: mentholated juniper, pineapple sage, lemon verbena, lavender, rose, shifting as it warms.
critics.palate: Minty and herbal with herbaceous juniper, blackthorn, lavender and pepper; thick, rich mouthfeel.
critics.finish: Oily aromatic herbs, peppermint, lemon balm and blackberry; fresh and fruity.
critics.summary: Main critique is that the contemporary profile sidelines juniper; still recommended as an indulgence.

facts.mash_bill: Molasses-based spirit; 47 botanicals incl. juniper, lingonberry, blackberry, pomelo, chamomile, sage, angelica, coriander, spruce
facts.cask: Earthenware vessels

ks-monkey-47-schwarzwalk-dry-gin.notes: Input name misspells Schwarzwald. Producer notes are a single descriptive sentence, not split nose/palate/finish. Region from Distiller/producer Black Forest framing.

producer.nose: Prominent Douglas fir and California bay laurel with subtle citrus.
producer.palate: Sage and wok-roasted coriander evoke hillside scrub; angelica root and Saigon cinnamon add earthy undertones.
producer.finish: Clean and crisp with forest-like complexity.
producer.summary: Woodsy, aromatic gin meant to evoke the California landscape. Fir and sage distilled separately; bay laurel and juniper vapor-infused; other botanicals in the pot.

critics.nose: Bold Douglas fir with sage growing more present over time.
critics.palate: Full-bodied; juniper subdued, little citrus.
critics.finish: Peppery.
critics.summary: Spicy, herbal gin suggested for a Gibson or Bramble.

critics.nose: Pine cones, pine needles and sage.
critics.palate: Brawny pine resin with eucalyptus and sage.
critics.finish: Bone dry with pine resin.
critics.summary: Fir-pine character leads over traditional juniper; unconventional but still gin-like.

critics.nose: Pine buds, spruce, fir and pine cones; immediately evocative.
critics.palate: Sage and bay leaf early, then juniper and fir needle turning minty; coriander, gentle spice and a touch of lemon.
critics.finish: Cool, moderately long, minty sage; very smooth.
critics.summary: Highly recommended; best neat or in a G&T with lime.

facts.mash_bill: Botanicals: Douglas fir, California bay laurel, juniper, wok-roasted coriander, lemon, Seville orange, angelica, orris, sage, Saigon cinnamon, cardamom, fennel
facts.cask: Fir and sage distilled separately; bay laurel and juniper vapor-infused

ks-st-george-terroir-gin.notes: ABV 45% confirmed by producer and Difford's.

producer.summary: Producer gives no formal tasting notes, only calls it very smooth and suitable neat or mixed. Botanicals: cardamom, coriander, French lavender, anise seed, sarsaparilla, juniper and two orange peels; 18-hour maceration then steam-heated distillation.

critics.nose: Sarsaparilla and orange peel that highlight lavender.
critics.palate: Subtle sweetness with juniper pine in a supporting role.
critics.finish: Bittersweet with cinnamon and minty notes.
critics.summary: Suggested for an Aviation, Pegu Club or Bee's Knees.

critics.nose: Faint juniper with coriander and star anise.
critics.palate: White pepper, orange oil and lavender; very gentle.
critics.finish: Tangy and gently expansive.
critics.summary: Rated 2 stars (Recommended) on the site's own star system; soft gin good neat or for vodka drinkers, easily lost in cocktails.

facts.mash_bill: 100% grain neutral spirit; botanicals cardamom, coriander, French lavender, anise seed, sarsaparilla, juniper, two orange peels
facts.cask: 18-hour botanical maceration, steam-heated still, heart cut

ks-aviation-american-gin.notes: No producer nose/palate/finish; critic notes only. Producer site lists Diageo as current owner/distiller.

producer.nose: Rich, inviting aroma of sweet, fresh apricot.
producer.palate: Voluptuous vanilla with mellow oak; smooth.
producer.summary: Producer page (V.S.O.P Privilège) describes a ruby-amber color, apricot nose and vanilla/oak palate; blend dates to 1817.

critics.nose: Highly aromatic, led by fruit that has moved toward dried fruit.
critics.summary: Expert review excerpt only partially captured.

critics.nose: Strong fruit bouquet with hints of honey.
critics.palate: Dominated by woody cask notes.
critics.finish: Woody.
critics.summary: Retailer/specialist site's own notes; its 3.5/5 is a user-review average so not recorded as a score.

facts.mash_bill: Blend of eaux-de-vie from Grande Champagne, Petite Champagne, Borderies and Fins Bois
facts.cask: French oak (Limousin per Cognac-Expert)

ks-hennessy-privilege-vsop-cognac.notes: Distiller's tasting text was only partially retrieved. Cru list from Distiller.

critics.nose: Lots of fruit and floral notes, a touch of wood and barrel spice, mostly sweet young fruit.
critics.summary: Youthful, fruit-forward VSOP.

critics.nose: Floral and fruity: plums edging to citrus, candied pineapple.
critics.palate: Spiced apples and pears, cinnamon, nutmeg, a hint of anise.
critics.finish: Short to moderate, drying, dark berries.
critics.summary: Whisky reviewer self-described as unfamiliar with cognac; preferred it to Courvoisier VS.

facts.age: NAS (VSOP; Distiller says eaux-de-vie aged 4-12 years)
facts.mash_bill: Fine Champagne cognac (Grande + Petite Champagne, ~55% Grande Champagne per Distiller); predominantly Ugni Blanc
facts.cask: Limousin oak

ks-remy-martin-vsop-cognac.notes: Producer page fetched but held no tasting notes. Difford's lists a 'Mature Cask Finish' VSOP, possibly a different market label, so not used. Cocktail Chemistry review blocked by redirect loop.

producer.palate: Subtle sweetness of vanilla, coconut and spice, generous with ginger and candied fruit, plum and toasted oak.
producer.summary: Martell VSOP eaux-de-vie (min. 4 years) finished in bourbon casks.

critics.palate: Sweet vanilla and a little smoke from American oak, then the brandy's fruit.
critics.summary: Dark color from bourbon-barrel finish; built to appeal to bourbon drinkers and blends both well.

facts.mash_bill: Blend from Borderies, Grande Champagne, Petite Champagne and Fins Bois (per Cognac-Expert)
facts.cask: French oak, finished in Kentucky bourbon casks

ks-martell-blue-swift-vsop-cognac.notes: Legally labeled as eau-de-vie in some markets due to bourbon cask finish. Cognac-Expert relays Martell notes (fresh perfume/mint nose; banana, vanilla, coconut, menthol; toasted oak).

critics.nose: Stewed prunes, vinous varnish, vanilla, fresh toast, spruce needles and toasted coconut with a sawn-wood note.
critics.palate: Light honeyed sweetness; delicate and easy sipping with cherry and gentle spice.
critics.finish: Lingering stewed and dried fruit with cherry wood and mild cinnamon.
critics.summary: Deep bronze-amber; easy-sipping XO. Sampled 2013.

facts.mash_bill: Estate-grown Ugni Blanc, Colombard, Baco and Folle Blanche
facts.cask: Gascon oak casks (400 L, made by the chateau's own cooper per Difford's)

ks-chateau-de-laubade-xo-armagnac.notes: Producer site unreachable. Master of Malt description (retailer) calls it rich and sweet with nutty notes, stewed plum and a hint of smoke. Natalie MacLean page showed only community notes, no score. Distiller page had no expert review.

producer.nose: Harmonious aroma of oak, berries and a light floral quality (retailer-relayed).
producer.palate: Light and vibrant.
producer.finish: Dry and spice-filled with subtle roasted notes.
producer.summary: Retailer (Spec's) relays these as producer notes; producer suggests it as an aperitif.

facts.mash_bill: California grape wines; sources disagree (Distiller: Colombard, Pinot Noir, Chenin Blanc; Spec's: mainly Pinot Noir with Colombard, Ehrenfelser)
facts.cask: Limousin oak

ks-germain-robin-craft-method-brandy.notes: Producer site no longer lists 'Craft Method' (now flagship 'Germain-Robin Brandy', unconfirmed as same product) so its notes were not used. Age conflicts: Distiller ~6 years (VSOP-equivalent, lot-numbered), Spec's 8-22 years. No critic reviews found.

producer.nose: Fresh and exuberant: passionfruit and lime zest with a herbal hint.
producer.palate: Tropical fruit, guava and pink grapefruit with lemongrass and bell pepper; mouth-watering acidity and minerality.
producer.summary: Producer notes shown for the 2024 vintage (latest on site); cool, slow stainless fermentation, 2024 blend includes some Awatere Valley fruit.

facts.cask: Cool stainless-steel fermentation

ks-stoneleigh-sauvignon-blanc.notes: Input vintage 2026 has no published notes; producer notes are for 2024. Producer lists awards (e.g. Tasting Panel 93 points, 2023) without clear vintage, so not recorded as critic scores.

producer.palate: Ripe passionfruit, pineapple, zesty citrus and fresh green herbs; crisp, vibrant tropical fruit.
producer.summary: Retailer (67 Wine) relays these as producer notes for the 2025 Marlborough wine.

ks-nobilo-sauvignon-blanc.notes: Vintage 2025. Only retailer-relayed producer text found; no critic reviews within budget.

critics.nose: Kaffir lime, passionfruit pulp and lemon zest.
critics.palate: Concentrated citrus and tropical fruit with salivating acidity.
critics.summary: Pale lime-straw. Article from 2021; vintage not stated.

critics.nose: Citrus up front: gooseberry, grapefruit, lemon zest, lime, pear, tropical fruit, lemongrass.
critics.palate: Medium-bodied, high acid, crisp and fruity.
critics.finish: Nice minerality balanced by acid.
critics.summary: 2016 review of an older vintage (page appears to say 2015); not the 2025.

ks-infamous-goose-sauvignon-blanc.notes: No critic or producer notes for the 2025 vintage; critic notes are from older/unspecified vintages.

producer.nose: Pungent sweet grass, nettles, blackcurrant and gooseberry.
producer.palate: Light-bodied.
producer.finish: Long, fine, appetizing mineral finish with ripe greens, gooseberry and currant.
producer.summary: Retailer (BuyWinesOnline) relays these as producer notes for the 2025; pale straw with green hues.

ks-sea-pearl-sauvignon-blanc.notes: Vintage 2025. Only retailer-relayed producer notes; no critic reviews found.

producer.nose: Fresh passion fruit, lime zest and gooseberry with bright intensity.
producer.palate: Crisp citrus with tropical mango and grapefruit.
producer.summary: US importer (Vintage Imports) sheet for the Estate Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc: cool-morning harvest, temperature-controlled stainless fermentation, brief lees ageing.

critics.nose: Passionfruit and green herb baseline.
critics.palate: Apple and citrus with pith and peel.
critics.finish: Steely, salivating, crisp and dry.
critics.summary: 2025 vintage; drink 2025-2027.

facts.cask: Stainless steel, brief fine-lees ageing

ks-ant-moore-sauvignon-blanc-estate-seri.notes: Critic review is titled 'Ant Moore Sauvignon Blanc 2025' without 'Estate Series'; assumed to be the core Estate bottling (Signature Series is labeled separately). Importer sheet gives 12.5% ABV vs label 12% and no vintage.

producer.palate: Crisp acidity, nuanced herbaceous character and an interplay of citrus and tropical fruit.
producer.summary: Retailer (CocoVino) product description for the 2023 Sonoma County bottling; not clearly attributed to the winery.

ks-girard-sauvignon-blanc.notes: Vintage 2023. Winery site gave no Sauvignon Blanc page. Another retailer (Blackwell's) listing titled 2023 Sonoma County shows Napa Valley estate notes and a Suckling review of the 2022 Napa wine, so not used due to appellation conflict.

producer.palate: Ripe guava, crushed pineapple, ruby grapefruit and fresh-cut grass; light and refreshing.
producer.summary: Retailer (Empire Wine) relays producer description for the 2024; low-calorie, zero-sugar, low-alcohol wine from Scheid Family Wines.

ks-sunny-with-a-chance-of-flowers-sauvig.notes: Vintage 2024. Retailer lists 85 calories per 5 oz. No critic reviews found.

producer.nose: White flowers and citrus.
producer.palate: Bright, round mouthfeel with tropical guava, Meyer lemon and key lime.
producer.summary: Winery page shows these notes for the 2023 vintage; a retailer (Empire Wine) relays the same notes for the 2025. Light straw color.

ks-raeburn-sauvignon-blanc.notes: Input vintage 2025; winery notes are for 2023 (retailer shows identical text for 2025). Winery cites James Suckling 90 (2023) and Tasting Panel 93 (2022), not recorded since critic pages weren't fetched and vintages differ.

producer.nose: Nectarine, lime, melon with subtle wet stone and flint.
producer.palate: Grapefruit and white peach with tropical mango and guava; crisp, vibrant acidity.
producer.summary: Winery notes for the 2024 Sonoma County Sauvignon Blanc; some barrel fermentation adds body and texture.

facts.cask: Partial barrel fermentation

ks-la-crema-sauvignon-blanc.notes: Vintage 2024. A Wine Enthusiast review of the 2024 exists but the page failed (redirect loop), so no critic data recorded.

ks-domaine-fouassier-sauvignon-blanc-les.notes: Vintage 2023. Only a retailer's in-house note (VinoVoss 'Voss Experts', 4.5/5): flinty minerality, citrus zest and white blossom; green apple, lime, subtle herbs; crisp saline mineral finish. Importer (Winebow) page timed out.

producer.nose: Fresh and inviting.
producer.palate: Crisp and refreshing with grapefruit and lemon, hints of tropical fruit and a subtle herbaceous note; light-bodied.
producer.summary: Retailer (Onshore Cellars) description of Joseph Mellot 'Sincérité' Sauvignon Blanc (listed as IGP Val de Loire, 2023/2024, 13.5%); not clearly attributed to the producer.

critics.palate: Lush, with citrus and lychee and a bitter note (excerpt only).
critics.summary: 2023 Vin de France Sincérité; score and full note paywalled. Published 2025.

ks-joseph-mellot-sauvignon-blanc.notes: Assumed to be the 'Sincérité' bottling (the producer's Vin de France Sauvignon Blanc per Wine Spectator). Input is 2021 at 12%; sources cover 2023/2024 and the retailer lists 13.5%.

critics.nose: Tarragon and fennel.
critics.palate: Bright peach and grapefruit with semi-bitter herbal and spice notes.
critics.finish: Focused minerality.
critics.summary: Reviewed the 2021 vintage (not 2020) in 2023; intense and focused for an entry-level estate bottling.

facts.mash_bill: 100% Sauvignon Blanc from ~55 plots; limestone and clay soils
facts.cask: Stainless steel

ks-weingut-tement-sauvignon-blanc-kalk-k.notes: Input vintage 2020; only critic note found is for 2021. Producer site (tement.at) unreachable. Facts relayed by the reviewer and may be vintage-specific; certified organic/biodynamic per reviewer.

producer.nose: Strong caramel and almond with dark fruit and figs.
producer.palate: Heavy dark fruit and tobacco rounded by caramel.
producer.summary: Barrel-proof Maker's 46 (proof varies roughly 107-114 by batch); fully matured Maker's finished with ten seared virgin French oak staves (Stave Profile No. 46).

critics.nose: Graham cracker, toasted oak and marshmallow, then toffee, caramel and bold cinnamon.
critics.palate: Sweet cinnamon, vanilla, light oak, wheat grain and honey; bold but balanced.
critics.finish: Heat, then cinnamon, honey and dry oak, settling to light oak.
critics.summary: 2021 release at 110.3 proof; competent but less distinctive than the 2015 original.

critics.nose: Deeper, dessert-like French oak character: vanilla, toffee, chocolate, fig, cherry.
critics.palate: Woody with white pepper, cinnamon, allspice and chai; chocolate and coffee bean, little fruit.
critics.finish: Oak-led and tannic with tobacco leaf, coffee bean and vanilla.
critics.summary: Compares favorably to other wheaters; proof of bottle not stated.

critics.nose: Soft caramel then strong vanilla, baking spice and oak.
critics.palate: Plastic note at first, then caramel, banana bread and cinnamon with sharp heat and a medicinal edge.
critics.finish: Medicinal notes linger.
critics.summary: Reviewed a 109.6-proof bottling; better as a mixer than a sipper.

facts.mash_bill: 70% corn, 16% red winter wheat, 14% malted barley
facts.cask: Finished with 10 seared virgin French oak staves inserted into matured barrels

ks-maker-s-mark-no-46-french-oaked-cask-.notes: Batch-variable proof; label is 110.6 but critics reviewed 110.3, 109.6 and an unstated proof. Mash bill from Breaking Bourbon.

critics.nose: Light cinnamon with vanilla, caramel and baking spice; fleeting oak and green apple.
critics.palate: Spicy baking-spice and cinnamon base balanced by caramel and light apple.
critics.finish: Brown sugar, apricot and oak with lingering light spice.
critics.summary: 80 proof; solid budget value, though the low proof limits flavor.

critics.nose: Raw corn, vanilla and caramel with faint citrus, spice and strawberry; waterlogged wood.
critics.palate: Dusty corn and vanilla with caramel and light spice; some astringent wood.
critics.finish: Medium, corn-forward with vanilla, spice and wet wood.
critics.summary: Light and simple; suggests the Bottled-in-Bond instead.

critics.nose: Heavy vanilla with caramel and rye bread.
critics.palate: Vanilla-forward with peppery spice and hints of toffee; better on ice.
critics.finish: Smooth and peppery with lingering spice.
critics.summary: Good value; high-rye mash shows in peppery notes, works in cocktails.

ks-old-grand-dad-old-grand-dad-ksbw.notes: Producer site unreachable; no producer notes recorded.

producer.nose: Dark fruit, vanilla and green apple.
producer.palate: Oak, toasted almond and toffee.
producer.summary: Jefferson's Reserve, now carrying an 8-year minimum age statement at 96 proof; blended from selected mature barrels.

ks-jefferson-s-8-yo-ksbw.notes: Identified as Jefferson's Reserve 8 Year. Critic reviews found (Distiller, Thirty One Whiskey) cover the older NAS 90.2-proof Jefferson's Reserve, so not used.

ks-hardin-s-creek-ksbw-middle-distillati.notes: Likely Hardin's Creek 8 Year 'Middle Distillation Profile' (2026 release calendar lists it at 115 proof, plus TTB-filed 700 mL versions at 109 proof). No producer or critic tasting notes found.

producer.nose: Cooked apple and caramel with soft oak.
producer.palate: Rich molasses, chocolate and barrel spice, coating the mouth.
producer.summary: First age-stated Jack Daniel's in over a century, released in batches since 2021; aged in handmade American white oak barrels.

critics.nose: Charred oak, light maple candy, baking spice, banana flambé, a hint of clove.
critics.palate: Rye and black peppercorn spice, banana, charred oak, dried tobacco, browned butter.
critics.finish: Peppery, dry charred oak, leather, tobacco, burnt caramel; noticeably dry.
critics.summary: Batch 5, 97 proof; solid but drier and less appealing than Batch 4.

critics.nose: Batch 5: apple pie with cinnamon, clove and ginger.
critics.palate: Batch 5: menthol-tinged gingerbread cake, rum raisin and apple butter.
critics.finish: Batch 5: sweet with balanced oak and tannin.
critics.summary: Covers all batches (all 97 proof); Batch 5 graded A (letter grade) and called the best of the series; earlier batches graded A- to B.

facts.cask: American white oak

ks-jack-daniel-s-10-years-old-tennessee-.notes: Batch of the Kansas bottle unknown; critic notes are for Batch 5 (2026).

producer.summary: Launch press release describes sweet, creamy notes of pipe tobacco, seasoned oak and butterscotch; charcoal mellowed before aging in new toasted and charred barrels. No separate nose/palate/finish given.

critics.nose: Tobacco, leather and toffee, with vanilla and candied strawberry developing in the glass.
critics.palate: Heavily oak-driven and tannic; water softens it to show cherry, cola, tobacco, leather, cinnamon, caraway and clove.
critics.finish: Medium length with a lingering smoky quality.
critics.summary: Prefers it to the 10 Year as extra age tames the sweetness, though the oak can dominate; reviewer's favorite current JD release.

critics.nose: Brown sugar butter, maple-soaked corn cakes, nuttiness, seasoned oak, brown spice and light vanilla.
critics.palate: Buttered grits, maple syrup, cinnamon-led baking spice, velvety oak, vanilla coffee and mashed banana; proof feels restrained.
critics.finish: Mellow with no burn; bruleed banana, caramel and butterscotch with subtle oak.
critics.summary: An easy, effortless drinker, though the reviewer feels the Lincoln County Process limits complexity.

facts.cask: New toasted and charred American white oak; charcoal mellowed before aging

ks-jack-daniel-s-12-years-old-tennessee-.notes: Producer info is the combined descriptor from the 2023 launch press release; jackdaniels.com product page returned 404.

producer.nose: Vanilla bean, Earl Grey tea, caramel and sweet tobacco.
producer.palate: Pecan pie, whole grain toast and grapefruit peel.
producer.finish: Nutmeg, birch beer and dry oak tannin.
producer.summary: Hyper-small-batch 13-year bourbon, non-chill filtered and proofed with Rosendale Mines limestone water.

critics.nose: Candied apple, cinnamon, nutmeg, clove and leather.
critics.palate: Tart red apple, vanilla, caramel, espresso, toasted oak and bitter chocolate.
critics.finish: Warm and spicy.
critics.summary: Fall 2021 small-batch release at 93 proof; profiled as spicy and rich.

ks-widow-jane-lucky-thirteen-small-batch.notes: Input lists 101 proof but producer page and Distiller list 93 proof; the Kansas label may be a different batch strength, so notes may not match exactly. Skipped Paste's 2020 review (earlier single-barrel, variable-proof version).

critics.nose: Port influence brings raisin and mint forward, with more clove than the unfinished bourbon.
critics.palate: Apple butter gives a rich mouthfeel; baking spice throughout.
critics.finish: Sweet with lingering baking spice; possibly too sweet for some drinkers.
critics.summary: Graded A- (letter grade). Reviewed at 90 proof, finished in 14-year-old ruby port casks.

critics.palate: Butterscotch, clove and banana bread.
critics.finish: Gentle fruity port notes add complexity without overwhelming the bourbon.
critics.summary: An appealing pairing of spicy bourbon and sweeter port character.

facts.cask: Finished in 14-year-old ruby port wine casks

ks-tom-s-town-distilling-co-pendergast-s.notes: Producer site unreachable (403/DNS); no producer notes. Facts from Drinkhacker (MGP sourcing is the reviewer's presumption). Input had no proof; 90 proof per Drinkhacker/Distiller.

producer.nose: Freshly brewed coffee and rich molasses with subtle sweet corn and spice.
producer.palate: Layered vanilla and young oak blending into milk chocolate.
producer.finish: Medium-long and balanced; oak and vanilla with a touch of dark roast coffee and brown spice.
producer.summary: Master blender Alan Kennedy's notes as relayed in launch press coverage (Northwest Beer Guide), not fetched from the brand site. Color described as deep amber.

facts.mash_bill: Corn, rye and barley (proportions not given); charcoal mellowed (Lincoln County Process)
facts.cask: Cold-steeped, custom-roasted Honduran Arabica coffee beans (Agalta region) introduced during final maturation

ks-bib-tucker-aged-6-years-gold-roast-bo.notes: 2025 coffee-infused release, sold as a bourbon flavored with coffee. No independent critic review fetched (Whiskey Apostle review timed out).

producer.nose: Toffee, honey and black walnut moving toward chocolate and caramel, with cherry, mint and strong rye spice (nose and palate described together).
producer.palate: Same combined description as nose: toffee, honey, black walnut, chocolate, caramel, cherry, mint and rye spice.
producer.finish: Oak and toastiness lead, lingering with warm gingerbread.
producer.summary: 2026 edition notes from michters.com; fully matured US*1 rye re-barreled in a custom toasted barrel of 24-month air-dried wood, bottled at barrel strength.

critics.nose: Black cherry and walnut like a fruit cobbler, then brown sugar, honey, molasses, toffee and taffy.
critics.palate: Toasted honey, pecan, semi-sweet chocolate, Derby-pie character, blackstrap molasses, then oak; apple pie spice for balance.
critics.finish: Hot and drying with oak, cinnamon gum and black pepper.
critics.summary: Wood-forward and possibly divisive but well made; good with dessert. 2023 release, sampled at 109.4 proof.

facts.cask: Finished in custom toasted (not charred) barrel from 24-month air-dried wood

ks-michter-s-barrel-strength-toasted-bar.notes: Barrel-strength proof varies by barrel/year; producer page is 2026 edition (avg 109.1), VinePair is 2023 edition, input label 108 proof. Producer notes combine nose and palate.

producer.nose: Oak, vanilla, sweet cream and fruitcake shifting to cinnamon, spice and florals.
producer.palate: Cherry, raisin and dark honey giving way to herbal clove, spearmint and thyme.
producer.finish: Long, with spice, mature oak, char and pepper.
producer.summary: Official 2024 Camp Nelson B release notes as relayed by Breaking Bourbon's press-release page; sixth-floor barrels, non-chill filtered, barrel proof, highest-proof Russell's Reserve to date.

critics.nose: Sweet oak, molasses and honeyed cornbread, nutmeg and boozy cherries, then spearmint and cocoa.
critics.palate: Syrupy honey, dark oak and tannin, brown butter, dark fruits (blackcurrant, prune, fig, cherry), chocolate and creamy peanut butter.
critics.finish: Long and oaky with cherry-cola notes; water brings out black cherry, dark grape and a brandy-like quality.
critics.summary: Reviewer's favorite of the three Single Rickhouse releases, narrowly ahead of Camp Nelson F.

critics.nose: Ethanol up front; with time, warm honey and golden raisins.
critics.palate: Apple, raisin, honey and lemon with crisp oak and restrained spice.
critics.finish: Long and warming with spice, oak, char and pepper, not overly dry.
critics.summary: Nothing to dislike except the steep price; rated 'Bar' on the site's buy/bar/bust scale.

facts.region: Kentucky (Camp Nelson B rickhouse, sixth floor)

ks-russell-s-reserve-single-rickhouse-ks.notes: Identified via 120.2 proof as the 2024 Camp Nelson B edition. Producer notes are relayed via Breaking Bourbon press release.

producer.nose: Citrus, floral and honey.
producer.palate: Citrus, burnt sugar, cinnamon, caramel and lemon zest.
producer.finish: Bourbon spice balanced against the Sauternes cask influence.
producer.summary: Producer notes as relayed by retailer Caskers (not fetched from jeffersonsbourbon.com, which returned 404). Finished in forty Chateau Suduiraut barrels in a 'hot box' warehouse.

facts.cask: New charred American oak, then several months in ex-Chateau Suduiraut Sauternes French oak casks in a heated 'hot box' warehouse; 40 barrels

ks-jefferson-s-grand-selection-chateau-s.notes: Label spelling 'Suduirait' is Chateau Suduiraut. No critic review obtained (Whiskey Were Here hit a redirect loop; Distiller has only a community rating).

critics.nose: Juniper-led with bright lime zest and hints of red grapefruit.
critics.palate: Bitter orange and lemon, then angelica and pink grapefruit, closing on creamy licorice root and piney juniper.
critics.finish: Long, moderately warm, with citrus zest and earthy undertones.
critics.summary: Highly recommended classic-style gin; suggested for martinis, Tom Collins, Corpse Reviver #2 and G&Ts.

critics.nose: Bold juniper and soft citrus: grapefruit, blood orange and finger lime with licorice candy and angelica.
critics.palate: Creamy and full-bodied with chamomile florals and dominant grapefruit; rich yet bright, earthy base.
critics.finish: Clean, licorice-led, with a spicy tingle.
critics.summary: Called outstanding: powerful yet structured, bolder and more citrus-forward than standard Tanqueray. Reviewed at 47.3%.

facts.mash_bill: Wheat base spirit; botanicals juniper, coriander, licorice, angelica, chamomile plus fresh whole lime, orange and grapefruit (citrus distilled separately)
facts.cask: Distilled in the small 'Tiny Ten' still (about 500 L per batch); unaged

ks-tanqueray-10-gin-tanqueray-10-gin.notes: Tanqueray producer page 404'd; no producer notes. Facts from The Gin is In (Tiny Ten batch size from 88 Bamboo). ABV 47.3% per 88 Bamboo.

producer.summary: Producer copy relayed on the Whisky Advocate store product page: rich, smooth and earthy with notable complexity; sweet orange in a blend with no bitter botanicals; green cardamom adds spicy, sweet floral notes. No nose/palate/finish split.

critics.nose: Classically juniper-forward with green pine, orange zest and a distinctive camphor note.
critics.palate: Bright, green pine moving to citrus and spice; vanilla custard with lemon and sweet orange, then cardamom, white pepper and cassia.
critics.finish: Long, with licorice root and nuttiness, moderate warmth, slight astringency and light sweetness.
critics.summary: A versatile classic for martinis, Negronis and Last Words; complex despite a short botanical list. Reviewed at 41.2%.

critics.palate: Less crisp than typical London Dry, earthier from heavier root botanicals, with smoother juniper.
critics.finish: Unusually long for a gin, dominated by licorice and angelica.
critics.summary: A distinctive, heritage-driven gin set apart from modern London Dry conventions.

facts.mash_bill: Grain spirit base; seven botanicals: juniper, coriander seed, orange peel, lemon peel, green cardamom, orris root, angelica root
facts.cask: One-shot distillation in a 160+ year-old still with short neck and sharply bent lye pipe; unaged

ks-plymouth-original-gin.notes: Producer site 404'd; producer copy is retailer-relayed and summary-only.

producer.summary: Trade sheet calls it a 'meadow in bloom': a balanced gin of 19 botanicals with herbaceous character, bright citrus and delicate florals, versatile in cocktails.

critics.nose: Balanced layers of soft juniper, pine resin, fennel, lime zest, pepper and baking spice.
critics.palate: Juniper berry moving into dry green herbs (cilantro, dill) with earthy dark licorice.
critics.finish: Long pine, mint and ginger with lemony hops, candied orange and lime.

ks-st-george-botanivore-gin.notes: Producer product page 404'd; producer info from trade-support PDF (summary only).

producer.palate: Warm and fruity yet clean.

critics.nose: Wood spice suggesting fresh-sanded oak and sandalwood, with cinnamon, butterscotch, honey and citrus zest.

critics.finish: Green grape, honey and butterscotch, then lingering wood spice, pepper, cinnamon and a hint of mint.

critics.nose: Ripe pear, wax, green grape and delicate florals.
critics.palate: Mint and crushed peanut on a creamy texture.
critics.summary: Fruity, floral and higher-proof than most VS cognacs; designed mainly for mixing.

facts.mash_bill: Grande Champagne cru; distilled in Charentais alembic
facts.cask: Limousin (French) oak

critics.palate: Round, well-balanced mouthfeel with great complexity.
critics.finish: Mellow and lightly smoky.
critics.summary: Highly complex, balanced old Grande Champagne blend.

critics.finish: Wood takes over: elegant but drying with pepper, spice, tobacco and lingering rancio.

facts.cask: French oak (Troncais oak per Malt Mileage)

ks-hine-triomphe-cognac.notes: Hine producer page rendered empty (JS) so no producer notes. Age of components varies by source; treat as approximate.

producer.palate: Fresh and well balanced.
producer.summary: Producer notes as relayed by The Whisky Exchange retailer page; amber to golden color.

critics.summary: Recommended for sipping and quality mixing. Reviewed at 40%; originally 2014, revised 2018.

critics.summary: Retailer staff note praising it as complex value for cocktails or neat sipping (Planteray-branded bottling).

facts.region: Caribbean, blended/bottled by Maison Ferrand, France

All At Sea review predates rename.
